units.leftText: Now there was a certain man of Ramathaim Zophim, of the hill country of Ephraim, and his name was Elkanah, the son of Jeroham, the son of Elihu, the son of Tohu, the son of Zuph, an Ephraimite.
units.rightText: Now there was a certain man of Ramathaim-zophim, of the hill-country of Ephraim, and his name was Elkanah, the son of Jeroham, the son of Elihu, the son of Tohu, the son of Zuph, an Ephraimite:

units.leftText: He had two wives. The name of one was Hannah, and the name of the other Peninnah. Peninnah had children, but Hannah had no children.
units.rightText: and he had two wives; the name of the one was Hannah, and the name of the other Peninnah: and Peninnah had children, but Hannah had no children.

units.leftText: This man went up out of his city from year to year to worship and to sacrifice to the LORD of Armies in Shiloh. The two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, priests to the LORD, were there.
units.rightText: And this man went up out of his city from year to year to worship and to sacrifice unto Jehovah of hosts in Shiloh. And the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, priests unto Jehovah, were there.
leftNotes: 1:3 When rendered in ALL CAPITAL LETTERS, “LORD” or “GOD” is the translation of God’s Proper Name (Hebrew “יהוה*”, usually pronounced Yahweh).

units.leftText: When the day came that Elkanah sacrificed, he gave portions to Peninnah his wife and to all her sons and her daughters;
units.rightText: And when the day came that Elkanah sacrificed, he gave to Peninnah his wife, and to all her sons and her daughters, portions:

units.leftText: but he gave a double portion to Hannah, for he loved Hannah, but the LORD had shut up her womb.
units.rightText: but unto Hannah he gave a double portion; for he loved Hannah, but Jehovah had shut up her womb.

units.leftText: Her rival provoked her severely, to irritate her, because the LORD had shut up her womb.
units.rightText: And her rival provoked her sore, to make her fret, because Jehovah had shut up her womb.

units.leftText: So year by year, when she went up to the LORD’s house, her rival provoked her. Therefore she wept, and didn’t eat.
units.rightText: And as he did so year by year, when she went up to the house of Jehovah, so she provoked her; therefore she wept, and did not eat.

units.leftText: Elkanah her husband said to her, “Hannah, why do you weep? Why don’t you eat? Why is your heart grieved? Am I not better to you than ten sons?”
units.rightText: And Elkanah her husband said unto her, Hannah, why weepest thou? and why eatest thou not? and why is thy heart grieved? am not I better to thee than ten sons?

units.leftText: So Hannah rose up after they had finished eating and drinking in Shiloh. Now Eli the priest was sitting on his seat by the doorpost of the LORD’s temple.
units.rightText: So Hannah rose up after they had eaten in Shiloh, and after they had drunk. Now Eli the priest was sitting upon his seat by the door-post of the temple of Jehovah.

units.leftText: She was in bitterness of soul, and prayed to the LORD, weeping bitterly.
units.rightText: And she was in bitterness of soul, and prayed unto Jehovah, and wept sore.

units.leftText: She vowed a vow, and said, “LORD of Armies, if you will indeed look at the affliction of your servant and remember me, and not forget your servant, but will give to your servant a boy, then I will give him to the LORD all the days of his life, and no razor shall come on his head.”
units.rightText: And she vowed a vow, and said, O Jehovah of hosts, if thou wilt indeed look on the affliction of thy handmaid, and remember me, and not forget thy handmaid, but wilt give unto thy handmaid a man-child, then I will give him unto Jehovah all the days of his life, and there shall no razor come upon his head.

units.leftText: As she continued praying before the LORD, Eli saw her mouth.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, as she continued praying before Jehovah, that Eli marked her mouth.

units.leftText: Now Hannah spoke in her heart. Only her lips moved, but her voice was not heard. Therefore Eli thought she was drunk.
units.rightText: Now Hannah, she spake in her heart; only her lips moved, but her voice was not heard: therefore Eli thought she had been drunken.

units.leftText: Eli said to her, “How long will you be drunk? Get rid of your wine!”
units.rightText: And Eli said unto her, How long wilt thou be drunken? put away thy wine from thee.

units.leftText: Hannah answered, “No, my lord, I am a woman of a sorrowful spirit. I have not been drinking wine or strong drink, but I poured out my soul before the LORD.
units.rightText: And Hannah answered and said, No, my lord, I am a woman of a sorrowful spirit: I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, but I poured out my soul before Jehovah.

units.leftText: Don’t consider your servant a wicked woman; for I have been speaking out of the abundance of my complaint and my provocation.”
units.rightText: Count not thy handmaid for a wicked woman; for out of the abundance of my complaint and my provocation have I spoken hitherto.

units.leftText: Then Eli answered, “Go in peace; and may the God of Israel grant your petition that you have asked of him.”
units.rightText: Then Eli answered and said, Go in peace; and the God of Israel grant thy petition that thou hast asked of him.
leftNotes: 1:17 The Hebrew word rendered “God” is “אֱלֹהִ֑ים*” (Elohim).

units.leftText: She said, “Let your servant find favor in your sight.” So the woman went her way and ate; and her facial expression wasn’t sad any more.
units.rightText: And she said, Let thy handmaid find favor in thy sight. So the woman went her way, and did eat; and her countenance was no more sad.

units.leftText: They rose up in the morning early and worshiped the LORD, then returned and came to their house to Ramah. Then Elkanah knew Hannah his wife; and the LORD remembered her.
units.rightText: And they rose up in the morning early, and worshipped before Jehovah, and returned, and came to their house to Ramah. And Elkanah knew Hannah his wife; and Jehovah remembered her;

units.leftText: When the time had come, Hannah conceived, and bore a son; and she named him Samuel, saying, “Because I have asked him of the LORD.”
units.rightText: and it came to pass, when the time was come about, that Hannah conceived, and bare a son; and she called his name Samuel, saying, Because I have asked him of Jehovah.
leftNotes: 1:20 Samuel sounds like the Hebrew for “heard by God.”

units.leftText: The man Elkanah, and all his house, went up to offer to the LORD the yearly sacrifice and his vow.
units.rightText: And the man Elkanah, and all his house, went up to offer unto Jehovah the yearly sacrifice, and his vow.

units.leftText: But Hannah didn’t go up, for she said to her husband, “Not until the child is weaned; then I will bring him, that he may appear before the LORD, and stay there forever.”
units.rightText: But Hannah went not up; for she said unto her husband, I will not go up until the child be weaned; and then I will bring him, that he may appear before Jehovah, and there abide for ever.

units.leftText: Elkanah her husband said to her, “Do what seems good to you. Wait until you have weaned him; only may the LORD establish his word.”
units.rightText: And Elkanah her husband said unto her, Do what seemeth thee good; tarry until thou have weaned him; only Jehovah establish his word. So the woman tarried and gave her son suck, until she weaned him.

units.leftText: When she had weaned him, she took him up with her, with three bulls, and one ephah of meal, and a container of wine, and brought him to the LORD’s house in Shiloh. The child was young.
units.rightText: And when she had weaned him, she took him up with her, with three bullocks, and one ephah of meal, and a bottle of wine, and brought him unto the house of Jehovah in Shiloh: and the child was young.
leftNotes: 1:24 1 ephah is about 22 liters or about 2/3 of a bushel

units.leftText: They killed the bull, and brought the child to Eli.
units.rightText: And they slew the bullock, and brought the child to Eli.

units.leftText: She said, “Oh, my lord, as your soul lives, my lord, I am the woman who stood by you here, praying to the LORD.
units.rightText: And she said, Oh, my lord, as thy soul liveth, my lord, I am the woman that stood by thee here, praying unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: I prayed for this child, and the LORD has given me my petition which I asked of him.
units.rightText: For this child I prayed; and Jehovah hath given me my petition which I asked of him:

units.leftText: Therefore I have also given him to the LORD. As long as he lives he is given to the LORD.” He worshiped the LORD there.
units.rightText: therefore also I have granted him to Jehovah; as long as he liveth he is granted to Jehovah. And he worshipped Jehovah there.

units.leftText: Hannah prayed, and said,
units.rightText: And Hannah prayed, and said:

units.leftText: There is no one as holy as the LORD,
units.rightText: There is none holy as Jehovah;

units.leftText: “Don’t keep talking so exceedingly proudly.
units.rightText: Talk no more so exceeding proudly;

units.leftText: “The bows of the mighty men are broken.
units.rightText: The bows of the mighty men are broken;

units.leftText: Those who were full have hired themselves out for bread.
units.rightText: They that were full have hired out themselves for bread;

units.leftText: “The LORD kills and makes alive.
units.rightText: Jehovah killeth, and maketh alive:

units.leftText: The LORD makes poor and makes rich.
units.rightText: Jehovah maketh poor, and maketh rich:

units.leftText: He raises up the poor out of the dust.
units.rightText: He raiseth up the poor out of the dust,

units.leftText: He will keep the feet of his holy ones,
units.rightText: He will keep the feet of his holy ones;

units.leftText: Those who strive with the LORD shall be broken to pieces.
units.rightText: They that strive with Jehovah shall be broken to pieces;

units.leftText: Elkanah went to Ramah to his house. The child served the LORD before Eli the priest.
units.rightText: And Elkanah went to Ramah to his house. And the child did minister unto Jehovah before Eli the priest.

units.leftText: Now the sons of Eli were wicked men. They didn’t know the LORD.
units.rightText: Now the sons of Eli were base men; they knew not Jehovah.

units.leftText: The custom of the priests with the people was that when anyone offered a sacrifice, the priest’s servant came while the meat was boiling, with a fork of three teeth in his hand;
units.rightText: And the custom of the priests with the people was, that, when any man offered sacrifice, the priest’s servant came, while the flesh was boiling, with a flesh-hook of three teeth in his hand;

units.leftText: and he stabbed it into the pan, or kettle, or cauldron, or pot. The priest took all that the fork brought up for himself. They did this to all the Israelites who came there to Shiloh.
units.rightText: and he struck it into the pan, or kettle, or caldron, or pot; all that the flesh-hook brought up the priest took therewith. So they did in Shiloh unto all the Israelites that came thither.

units.leftText: Yes, before they burned the fat, the priest’s servant came, and said to the man who sacrificed, “Give meat to roast for the priest; for he will not accept boiled meat from you, but raw.”
units.rightText: Yea, before they burnt the fat, the priest’s servant came, and said to the man that sacrificed, Give flesh to roast for the priest; for he will not have boiled flesh of thee, but raw.

units.leftText: If the man said to him, “Let the fat be burned first, and then take as much as your soul desires;” then he would say, “No, but you shall give it to me now; and if not, I will take it by force.”
units.rightText: And if the man said unto him, They will surely burn the fat first, and then take as much as thy soul desireth; then he would say, Nay, but thou shalt give it me now: and if not, I will take it by force.

units.leftText: The sin of the young men was very great before the LORD; for the men despised the LORD’s offering.
units.rightText: And the sin of the young men was very great before Jehovah; for the men despised the offering of Jehovah.

units.leftText: But Samuel ministered before the LORD, being a child, clothed with a linen ephod.
units.rightText: But Samuel ministered before Jehovah, being a child, girded with a linen ephod.

units.leftText: Moreover his mother made him a little robe, and brought it to him from year to year when she came up with her husband to offer the yearly sacrifice.
units.rightText: Moreover his mother made him a little robe, and brought it to him from year to year, when she came up with her husband to offer the yearly sacrifice.

units.leftText: Eli blessed Elkanah and his wife, and said, “May the LORD give you offspring from this woman for the petition which was asked of the LORD.” Then they went to their own home.
units.rightText: And Eli blessed Elkanah and his wife, and said, Jehovah give thee seed of this woman for the petition which was asked of Jehovah. And they went unto their own home.
leftNotes: 2:20 or, seed

units.leftText: The LORD visited Hannah, and she conceived and bore three sons and two daughters. The child Samuel grew before the LORD.
units.rightText: And Jehovah visited Hannah, and she conceived, and bare three sons and two daughters. And the child Samuel grew before Jehovah.

units.leftText: Now Eli was very old; and he heard all that his sons did to all Israel, and how that they slept with the women who served at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
units.rightText: Now Eli was very old; and he heard all that his sons did unto all Israel, and how that they lay with the women that did service at the door of the tent of meeting.

units.leftText: He said to them, “Why do you do such things? For I hear of your evil dealings from all these people.
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Why do ye such things? for I hear of your evil dealings from all this people.

units.leftText: No, my sons; for it is not a good report that I hear! You make the LORD’s people disobey.
units.rightText: Nay, my sons; for it is no good report that I hear: ye make Jehovah’s people to transgress.

units.leftText: If one man sins against another, God will judge him; but if a man sins against the LORD, who will intercede for him?” Notwithstanding, they didn’t listen to the voice of their father, because the LORD intended to kill them.
units.rightText: If one man sin against another, God shall judge him; but if a man sin against Jehovah, who shall entreat for him? Notwithstanding, they hearkened not unto the voice of their father, because Jehovah was minded to slay them.

units.leftText: The child Samuel grew on, and increased in favor both with the LORD and also with men.
units.rightText: And the child Samuel grew on, and increased in favor both with Jehovah, and also with men.

units.leftText: A man of God came to Eli and said to him, “The LORD says, ‘Did I reveal myself to the house of your father when they were in Egypt in bondage to Pharaoh’s house?
units.rightText: And there came a man of God unto Eli, and said unto him, Thus saith Jehovah, Did I reveal myself unto the house of thy father, when they were in Egypt in bondage to Pharaoh’s house?

units.leftText: Didn’t I choose him out of all the tribes of Israel to be my priest, to go up to my altar, to burn incense, to wear an ephod before me? Didn’t I give to the house of your father all the offerings of the children of Israel made by fire?
units.rightText: and did I choose him out of all the tribes of Israel to be my priest, to go up unto mine altar, to burn incense, to wear an ephod before me? and did I give unto the house of thy father all the offerings of the children of Israel made by fire?

units.leftText: Why do you kick at my sacrifice and at my offering, which I have commanded in my habitation, and honor your sons above me, to make yourselves fat with the best of all the offerings of Israel my people?’
units.rightText: Wherefore kick ye at my sacrifice and at mine offering, which I have commanded in my habitation, and honorest thy sons above me, to make yourselves fat with the chiefest of all the offerings of Israel my people?

units.leftText: “Therefore the LORD, the God of Israel, says, ‘I said indeed that your house and the house of your father should walk before me forever.’ But now the LORD says, ‘Far be it from me; for those who honor me I will honor, and those who despise me will be cursed.
units.rightText: Therefore Jehovah, the God of Israel, saith, I said indeed that thy house, and the house of thy father, should walk before me for ever: but now Jehovah saith, Be it far from me; for them that honor me I will honor, and they that despise me shall be lightly esteemed.

units.leftText: Behold, the days come that I will cut off your arm and the arm of your father’s house, that there will not be an old man in your house.
units.rightText: Behold, the days come, that I will cut off thine arm, and the arm of thy father’s house, that there shall not be an old man in thy house.
leftNotes: 2:31 “Behold”, from “הִנֵּה*”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection.

units.leftText: You will see the affliction of my habitation, in all the wealth which I will give Israel. There shall not be an old man in your house forever.
units.rightText: And thou shalt behold the affliction of my habitation, in all the wealth which God shall give Israel; and there shall not be an old man in thy house for ever.

units.leftText: The man of yours whom I don’t cut off from my altar will consume your eyes and grieve your heart. All the increase of your house will die in the flower of their age.
units.rightText: And the man of thine, whom I shall not cut off from mine altar, shall be to consume thine eyes, and to grieve thy heart; and all the increase of thy house shall die in the flower of their age.
leftNotes: 2:33 or, blind your eyes with tears

units.leftText: This will be the sign to you that will come on your two sons, on Hophni and Phinehas: in one day they will both die.
units.rightText: And this shall be the sign unto thee, that shall come upon thy two sons, on Hophni and Phinehas: in one day they shall die both of them.

units.leftText: I will raise up a faithful priest for myself who will do according to that which is in my heart and in my mind. I will build him a sure house. He will walk before my anointed forever.
units.rightText: And I will raise me up a faithful priest, that shall do according to that which is in my heart and in my mind: and I will build him a sure house; and he shall walk before mine anointed for ever.

units.leftText: It will happen that everyone who is left in your house will come and bow down to him for a piece of silver and a loaf of bread, and will say, “Please put me into one of the priests’ offices, that I may eat a morsel of bread.”’”
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass, that every one that is left in thy house shall come and bow down to him for a piece of silver and a loaf of bread, and shall say, Put me, I pray thee, into one of the priests’ offices, that I may eat a morsel of bread.

units.leftText: The child Samuel ministered to the LORD before Eli. The LORD’s word was rare in those days. There were not many visions, then.
units.rightText: And the child Samuel ministered unto Jehovah before Eli. And the word of Jehovah was precious in those days; there was no frequent vision.

units.leftText: At that time, when Eli was laid down in his place (now his eyes had begun to grow dim, so that he could not see),
units.rightText: And it came to pass at that time, when Eli was laid down in his place (now his eyes had begun to wax dim, so that he could not see),

units.leftText: and God’s lamp hadn’t yet gone out, and Samuel had laid down in the LORD’s temple where God’s ark was,
units.rightText: and the lamp of God was not yet gone out, and Samuel was laid down to sleep, in the temple of Jehovah, where the ark of God was;

units.leftText: The LORD called Samuel. He said, “Here I am.”
units.rightText: that Jehovah called Samuel: and he said, Here am I.

units.leftText: He ran to Eli and said, “Here I am; for you called me.”
units.rightText: And he ran unto Eli, and said, Here am I; for thou calledst me. And he said, I called not; lie down again. And he went and lay down.

units.leftText: The LORD called yet again, “Samuel!”
units.rightText: And Jehovah called yet again, Samuel. And Samuel arose and went to Eli, and said, Here am I; for thou calledst me. And he answered, I called not, my son; lie down again.

units.leftText: Now Samuel didn’t yet know the LORD, neither was the LORD’s word yet revealed to him.
units.rightText: Now Samuel did not yet know Jehovah, neither was the word of Jehovah yet revealed unto him.

units.leftText: The LORD called Samuel again the third time. He arose and went to Eli and said, “Here I am; for you called me.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah called Samuel again the third time. And he arose and went to Eli, and said, Here am I; for thou calledst me. And Eli perceived that Jehovah had called the child.

units.leftText: Therefore Eli said to Samuel, “Go, lie down. It shall be, if he calls you, that you shall say, ‘Speak, LORD; for your servant hears.’” So Samuel went and lay down in his place.
units.rightText: Therefore Eli said unto Samuel, Go, lie down: and it shall be, if he call thee, that thou shalt say, Speak, Jehovah; for thy servant heareth. So Samuel went and lay down in his place.

units.leftText: The LORD came, and stood, and called as at other times, “Samuel! Samuel!”
units.rightText: And Jehovah came, and stood, and called as at other times, Samuel, Samuel. Then Samuel said, Speak; for thy servant heareth.

units.leftText: The LORD said to Samuel, “Behold, I will do a thing in Israel at which both the ears of everyone who hears it will tingle.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said to Samuel, Behold, I will do a thing in Israel, at which both the ears of every one that heareth it shall tingle.

units.leftText: In that day I will perform against Eli all that I have spoken concerning his house, from the beginning even to the end.
units.rightText: In that day I will perform against Eli all that I have spoken concerning his house, from the beginning even unto the end.

units.leftText: For I have told him that I will judge his house forever for the iniquity which he knew, because his sons brought a curse on themselves, and he didn’t restrain them.
units.rightText: For I have told him that I will judge his house for ever, for the iniquity which he knew, because his sons did bring a curse upon themselves, and he restrained them not.

units.leftText: Therefore I have sworn to the house of Eli that the iniquity of Eli’s house shall not be removed with sacrifice or offering forever.”
units.rightText: And therefore I have sworn unto the house of Eli, that the iniquity of Eli’s house shall not be expiated with sacrifice nor offering for ever.

units.leftText: Samuel lay until the morning, and opened the doors of the LORD’s house. Samuel was afraid to show Eli the vision.
units.rightText: And Samuel lay until the morning, and opened the doors of the house of Jehovah. And Samuel feared to show Eli the vision.

units.leftText: Then Eli called Samuel and said, “Samuel, my son!”
units.rightText: Then Eli called Samuel, and said, Samuel, my son. And he said, Here am I.

units.leftText: He said, “What is the thing that he has spoken to you? Please don’t hide it from me. God do so to you, and more also, if you hide anything from me of all the things that he spoke to you.”
units.rightText: And he said, What is the thing that Jehovah hath spoken unto thee? I pray thee, hide it not from me: God do so to thee, and more also, if thou hide anything from me of all the things that he spake unto thee.

units.leftText: Samuel told him every bit, and hid nothing from him.
units.rightText: And Samuel told him every whit, and hid nothing from him. And he said, It is Jehovah: let him do what seemeth him good.

units.leftText: Samuel grew, and the LORD was with him and let none of his words fall to the ground.
units.rightText: And Samuel grew, and Jehovah was with him, and did let none of his words fall to the ground.

units.leftText: All Israel from Dan even to Beersheba knew that Samuel was established to be a prophet of the LORD.
units.rightText: And all Israel from Dan even to Beer-sheba knew that Samuel was established to be a prophet of Jehovah.

units.leftText: The LORD appeared again in Shiloh; for the LORD revealed himself to Samuel in Shiloh by the LORD’s word.
units.rightText: And Jehovah appeared again in Shiloh; for Jehovah revealed himself to Samuel in Shiloh by the word of Jehovah.

units.leftText: The word of Samuel came to all Israel.
units.rightText: And the word of Samuel came to all Israel.

units.leftText: The Philistines put themselves in array against Israel. When they joined battle, Israel was defeated by the Philistines, who killed about four thousand men of the army in the field.
units.rightText: And the Philistines put themselves in array against Israel: and when they joined battle, Israel was smitten before the Philistines; and they slew of the army in the field about four thousand men.

units.leftText: When the people had come into the camp, the elders of Israel said, “Why has the LORD defeated us today before the Philistines? Let’s get the ark of the LORD’s covenant out of Shiloh and bring it to us, that it may come among us and save us out of the hand of our enemies.”
units.rightText: And when the people were come into the camp, the elders of Israel said, Wherefore hath Jehovah smitten us to-day before the Philistines? Let us fetch the ark of the covenant of Jehovah out of Shiloh unto us, that it may come among us, and save us out of the hand of our enemies.

units.leftText: So the people sent to Shiloh, and they brought from there the ark of the covenant of the LORD of Armies, who sits above the cherubim; and the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were there with the ark of the covenant of God.
units.rightText: So the people sent to Shiloh; and they brought from thence the ark of the covenant of Jehovah of hosts, who sitteth above the cherubim: and the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were there with the ark of the covenant of God.

units.leftText: When the ark of the LORD’s covenant came into the camp, all Israel shouted with a great shout, so that the earth resounded.
units.rightText: And when the ark of the covenant of Jehovah came into the camp, all Israel shouted with a great shout, so that the earth rang again.

units.leftText: When the Philistines heard the noise of the shout, they said, “What does the noise of this great shout in the camp of the Hebrews mean?” They understood that the LORD’s ark had come into the camp.
units.rightText: And when the Philistines heard the noise of the shout, they said, What meaneth the noise of this great shout in the camp of the Hebrews? And they understood that the ark of Jehovah was come into the camp.

units.leftText: The Philistines were afraid, for they said, “God has come into the camp.” They said, “Woe to us! For there has not been such a thing before.
units.rightText: And the Philistines were afraid, for they said, God is come into the camp. And they said, Woe unto us! for there hath not been such a thing heretofore.

units.leftText: Woe to us! Who shall deliver us out of the hand of these mighty gods? These are the gods that struck the Egyptians with all kinds of plagues in the wilderness.
units.rightText: Woe unto us! who shall deliver us out of the hand of these mighty gods? these are the gods that smote the Egyptians with all manner of plagues in the wilderness.

units.leftText: Be strong and behave like men, O you Philistines, that you not be servants to the Hebrews, as they have been to you. Strengthen yourselves like men, and fight!”
units.rightText: Be strong, and quit yourselves like men, O ye Philistines, that ye be not servants unto the Hebrews, as they have been to you: quit yourselves like men, and fight.

units.leftText: The Philistines fought, and Israel was defeated, and each man fled to his tent. There was a very great slaughter; for thirty thousand footmen of Israel fell.
units.rightText: And the Philistines fought, and Israel was smitten, and they fled every man to his tent: and there was a very great slaughter; for there fell of Israel thirty thousand footmen.

units.leftText: God’s ark was taken; and the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were slain.
units.rightText: And the ark of God was taken; and the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were slain.

units.leftText: A man of Benjamin ran out of the army and came to Shiloh the same day, with his clothes torn and with dirt on his head.
units.rightText: And there ran a man of Benjamin out of the army, and came to Shiloh the same day, with his clothes rent, and with earth upon his head.

units.leftText: When he came, behold, Eli was sitting on his seat by the road watching, for his heart trembled for God’s ark. When the man came into the city and told about it, all the city cried out.
units.rightText: And when he came, lo, Eli was sitting upon his seat by the wayside watching; for his heart trembled for the ark of God. And when the man came into the city, and told it, all the city cried out.

units.leftText: When Eli heard the noise of the crying, he said, “What does the noise of this tumult mean?”
units.rightText: And when Eli heard the noise of the crying, he said, What meaneth the noise of this tumult? And the man hasted, and came and told Eli.

units.leftText: Now Eli was ninety-eight years old. His eyes were set, so that he could not see.
units.rightText: Now Eli was ninety and eight years old; and his eyes were set, so that he could not see.

units.leftText: The man said to Eli, “I am he who came out of the army, and I fled today out of the army.”
units.rightText: And the man said unto Eli, I am he that came out of the army, and I fled to-day out of the army. And he said, How went the matter, my son?

units.leftText: He who brought the news answered, “Israel has fled before the Philistines, and there has been also a great slaughter among the people. Your two sons also, Hophni and Phinehas, are dead, and God’s ark has been captured.”
units.rightText: And he that brought the tidings answered and said, Israel is fled before the Philistines, and there hath been also a great slaughter among the people, and thy two sons also, Hophni and Phinehas, are dead, and the ark of God is taken.

units.leftText: When he made mention of God’s ark, Eli fell from off his seat backward by the side of the gate; and his neck broke, and he died, for he was an old man and heavy. He had judged Israel forty years.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when he made mention of the ark of God, that Eli fell from off his seat backward by the side of the gate; and his neck brake, and he died: for he was an old man, and heavy. And he had judged Israel forty years.

units.leftText: His daughter-in-law, Phinehas’ wife, was with child, near to giving birth. When she heard the news that God’s ark was taken and that her father-in-law and her husband were dead, she bowed herself and gave birth; for her pains came on her.
units.rightText: And his daughter-in-law, Phinehas’ wife, was with child, near to be delivered: and when she heard the tidings that the ark of God was taken, and that her father-in-law and her husband were dead, she bowed herself and brought forth; for her pains came upon her.

units.leftText: About the time of her death the women who stood by her said to her, “Don’t be afraid, for you have given birth to a son.” But she didn’t answer, neither did she regard it.
units.rightText: And about the time of her death the women that stood by her said unto her, Fear not; for thou hast brought forth a son. But she answered not, neither did she regard it.

units.leftText: She named the child Ichabod, saying, “The glory has departed from Israel!” because God’s ark was taken, and because of her father-in-law and her husband.
units.rightText: And she named the child Ichabod, saying, The glory is departed from Israel; because the ark of God was taken, and because of her father-in-law and her husband.
leftNotes: 4:21 “Ichabod” means “no glory”.

units.leftText: She said, “The glory has departed from Israel; for God’s ark has been taken.”
units.rightText: And she said, The glory is departed from Israel; for the ark of God is taken.

units.leftText: Now the Philistines had taken God’s ark, and they brought it from Ebenezer to Ashdod.
units.rightText: Now the Philistines had taken the ark of God, and they brought it from Eben-ezer unto Ashdod.

units.leftText: The Philistines took God’s ark, and brought it into the house of Dagon and set it by Dagon.
units.rightText: And the Philistines took the ark of God, and brought it into the house of Dagon, and set it by Dagon.

units.leftText: When the people of Ashdod arose early on the next day, behold, Dagon had fallen on his face to the ground before the LORD’s ark. They took Dagon and set him in his place again.
units.rightText: And when they of Ashdod arose early on the morrow, behold, Dagon was fallen upon his face to the ground before the ark of Jehovah. And they took Dagon, and set him in his place again.

units.leftText: When they arose early on the following morning, behold, Dagon had fallen on his face to the ground before the LORD’s ark; and the head of Dagon and both the palms of his hands were cut off on the threshold. Only Dagon’s torso was intact.
units.rightText: And when they arose early on the morrow morning, behold, Dagon was fallen upon his face to the ground before the ark of Jehovah; and the head of Dagon and both the palms of his hands lay cut off upon the threshold; only the stump of Dagon was left to him.

units.leftText: Therefore neither the priests of Dagon nor any who come into Dagon’s house step on the threshold of Dagon in Ashdod to this day.
units.rightText: Therefore neither the priests of Dagon, nor any that come into Dagon’s house, tread on the threshold of Dagon in Ashdod, unto this day.

units.leftText: But the LORD’s hand was heavy on the people of Ashdod, and he destroyed them and struck them with tumors, even Ashdod and its borders.
units.rightText: But the hand of Jehovah was heavy upon them of Ashdod, and he destroyed them, and smote them with tumors, even Ashdod and the borders thereof.

units.leftText: When the men of Ashdod saw that it was so, they said, “The ark of the God of Israel shall not stay with us, for his hand is severe on us and on Dagon our god.”
units.rightText: And when the men of Ashdod saw that it was so, they said, The ark of the God of Israel shall not abide with us; for his hand is sore upon us, and upon Dagon our god.

units.leftText: They sent therefore and gathered together all the lords of the Philistines, and said, “What shall we do with the ark of the God of Israel?”
units.rightText: They sent therefore and gathered all the lords of the Philistines unto them, and said, What shall we do with the ark of the God of Israel? And they answered, Let the ark of the God of Israel be carried about unto Gath. And they carried the ark of the God of Israel thither.

units.leftText: It was so, that after they had carried it there, the LORD’s hand was against the city with a very great confusion; and he struck the men of the city, both small and great, so that tumors broke out on them.
units.rightText: And it was so, that, after they had carried it about, the hand of Jehovah was against the city with a very great discomfiture: and he smote the men of the city, both small and great; and tumors brake out upon them.

units.leftText: So they sent God’s ark to Ekron.
units.rightText: So they sent the ark of God to Ekron. And it came to pass, as the ark of God came to Ekron, that the Ekronites cried out, saying, They have brought about the ark of the God of Israel to us, to slay us and our people.

units.leftText: They sent therefore and gathered together all the lords of the Philistines, and they said, “Send the ark of the God of Israel away, and let it go again to its own place, that it not kill us and our people.” For there was a deadly panic throughout all the city. The hand of God was very heavy there.
units.rightText: They sent therefore and gathered together all the lords of the Philistines, and they said, Send away the ark of the God of Israel, and let it go again to its own place, that it slay us not, and our people. For there was a deadly discomfiture throughout all the city; the hand of God was very heavy there.

units.leftText: The men who didn’t die were struck with the tumors; and the cry of the city went up to heaven.
units.rightText: And the men that died not were smitten with the tumors; and the cry of the city went up to heaven.

units.leftText: The LORD’s ark was in the country of the Philistines seven months.
units.rightText: And the ark of Jehovah was in the country of the Philistines seven months.

units.leftText: The Philistines called for the priests and the diviners, saying, “What shall we do with the LORD’s ark? Show us how we should send it to its place.”
units.rightText: And the Philistines called for the priests and the diviners, saying, What shall we do with the ark of Jehovah? show us wherewith we shall send it to its place.

units.leftText: They said, “If you send away the ark of the God of Israel, don’t send it empty; but by all means return a trespass offering to him. Then you will be healed, and it will be known to you why his hand is not removed from you.”
units.rightText: And they said, If ye send away the ark of the God of Israel, send it not empty; but by all means return him a trespass-offering: then ye shall be healed, and it shall be known to you why his hand is not removed from you.

units.leftText: Then they said, “What should the trespass offering be which we shall return to him?”
units.rightText: Then said they, What shall be the trespass-offering which we shall return to him? And they said, Five golden tumors, and five golden mice, according to the number of the lords of the Philistines; for one plague was on you all, and on your lords.

units.leftText: Therefore you shall make images of your tumors and images of your mice that mar the land; and you shall give glory to the God of Israel. Perhaps he will release his hand from you, from your gods, and from your land.
units.rightText: Wherefore ye shall make images of your tumors, and images of your mice that mar the land; and ye shall give glory unto the God of Israel: peradventure he will lighten his hand from off you, and from off your gods, and from off your land.

units.leftText: Why then do you harden your hearts as the Egyptians and Pharaoh hardened their hearts? When he had worked wonderfully among them, didn’t they let the people go, and they departed?
units.rightText: Wherefore then do ye harden your hearts, as the Egyptians and Pharaoh hardened their hearts? When he had wrought wonderfully among them, did they not let the people go, and they departed?

units.leftText: “Now therefore take and prepare yourselves a new cart and two milk cows on which there has come no yoke; and tie the cows to the cart, and bring their calves home from them;
units.rightText: Now therefore take and prepare you a new cart, and two milch kine, on which there hath come no yoke; and tie the kine to the cart, and bring their calves home from them;

units.leftText: and take the LORD’s ark and lay it on the cart. Put the jewels of gold, which you return him for a trespass offering, in a box by its side; and send it away, that it may go.

units.leftText: Behold, if it goes up by the way of its own border to Beth Shemesh, then he has done us this great evil; but if not, then we shall know that it is not his hand that struck us. It was a chance that happened to us.”
units.rightText: And see; if it goeth up by the way of its own border to Beth-shemesh, then he hath done us this great evil: but if not, then we shall know that it is not his hand that smote us; it was a chance that happened to us.

units.leftText: The men did so, and took two milk cows and tied them to the cart, and shut up their calves at home.
units.rightText: And the men did so, and took two milch kine, and tied them to the cart, and shut up their calves at home;

units.leftText: They put the LORD’s ark on the cart, and the box with the golden mice and the images of their tumors.
units.rightText: and they put the ark of Jehovah upon the cart, and the coffer with the mice of gold and the images of their tumors.

units.leftText: The cows took the straight way by the way to Beth Shemesh. They went along the highway, lowing as they went, and didn’t turn away to the right hand or to the left; and the lords of the Philistines went after them to the border of Beth Shemesh.
units.rightText: And the kine took the straight way by the way to Beth-shemesh; they went along the highway, lowing as they went, and turned not aside to the right hand or to the left; and the lords of the Philistines went after them unto the border of Beth-shemesh.

units.leftText: The people of Beth Shemesh were reaping their wheat harvest in the valley; and they lifted up their eyes and saw the ark, and rejoiced to see it.
units.rightText: And they of Beth-shemesh were reaping their wheat harvest in the valley; and they lifted up their eyes, and saw the ark, and rejoiced to see it.

units.leftText: The cart came into the field of Joshua of Beth Shemesh, and stood there, where there was a great stone. Then they split the wood of the cart and offered up the cows for a burnt offering to the LORD.
units.rightText: And the cart came into the field of Joshua the Beth-shemite, and stood there, where there was a great stone: and they clave the wood of the cart, and offered up the kine for a burnt-offering unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: The Levites took down the LORD’s ark and the box that was with it, in which the jewels of gold were, and put them on the great stone; and the men of Beth Shemesh offered burnt offerings and sacrificed sacrifices the same day to the LORD.
units.rightText: And the Levites took down the ark of Jehovah, and the coffer that was with it, wherein the jewels of gold were, and put them on the great stone: and the men of Beth-shemesh offered burnt-offerings and sacrificed sacrifices the same day unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: When the five lords of the Philistines had seen it, they returned to Ekron the same day.
units.rightText: And when the five lords of the Philistines had seen it, they returned to Ekron the same day.

units.leftText: These are the golden tumors which the Philistines returned for a trespass offering to the LORD: for Ashdod one, for Gaza one, for Ashkelon one, for Gath one, for Ekron one;
units.rightText: And these are the golden tumors which the Philistines returned for a trespass-offering unto Jehovah: for Ashdod one, for Gaza one, for Ashkelon one, for Gath one, for Ekron one;

units.leftText: and the golden mice, according to the number of all the cities of the Philistines belonging to the five lords, both of fortified cities and of country villages, even to the great stone on which they set down the LORD’s ark. That stone remains to this day in the field of Joshua of Beth Shemesh.
units.rightText: and the golden mice, according to the number of all the cities of the Philistines belonging to the five lords, both of fortified cities and of country villages, even unto the great stone, whereon they set down the ark of Jehovah, which stone remaineth unto this day in the field of Joshua the Beth-shemite.

units.leftText: He struck of the men of Beth Shemesh, because they had looked into the LORD’s ark, he struck fifty thousand seventy of the men. Then the people mourned, because the LORD had struck the people with a great slaughter.
units.rightText: And he smote of the men of Beth-shemesh, because they had looked into the ark of Jehovah, he smote of the people seventy men, and fifty thousand men; and the people mourned, because Jehovah had smitten the people with a great slaughter.

units.leftText: The men of Beth Shemesh said, “Who is able to stand before the LORD, this holy God? To whom shall he go up from us?”
units.rightText: And the men of Beth-shemesh said, Who is able to stand before Jehovah, this holy God? and to whom shall he go up from us?

units.leftText: They sent messengers to the inhabitants of Kiriath Jearim, saying, “The Philistines have brought back the LORD’s ark. Come down and bring it up to yourselves.”
units.rightText: And they sent messengers to the inhabitants of Kiriath-jearim, saying, The Philistines have brought back the ark of Jehovah; come ye down, and fetch it up to you.

units.leftText: The men of Kiriath Jearim came and took the LORD’s ark, and brought it into Abinadab’s house on the hill, and consecrated Eleazar his son to keep the LORD’s ark.
units.rightText: And the men of Kiriath-jearim came, and fetched up the ark of Jehovah, and brought it into the house of Abinadab in the hill, and sanctified Eleazar his son to keep the ark of Jehovah.

units.leftText: From the day that the ark stayed in Kiriath Jearim, the time was long—for it was twenty years; and all the house of Israel lamented after the LORD.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, from the day that the ark abode in Kiriath-jearim, that the time was long; for it was twenty years: and all the house of Israel lamented after Jehovah.

units.leftText: Samuel spoke to all the house of Israel, saying, “If you are returning to the LORD with all your heart, then put away the foreign gods and the Ashtaroth from among you, and direct your hearts to the LORD, and serve him only; and he will deliver you out of the hand of the Philistines.”
units.rightText: And Samuel spake unto all the house of Israel, saying, If ye do return unto Jehovah with all your heart, then put away the foreign gods and the Ashtaroth from among you, and direct your hearts unto Jehovah, and serve him only; and he will deliver you out of the hand of the Philistines.

units.leftText: Then the children of Israel removed the Baals and the Ashtaroth, and served the LORD only.
units.rightText: Then the children of Israel did put away the Baalim and the Ashtaroth, and served Jehovah only.

units.leftText: Samuel said, “Gather all Israel to Mizpah, and I will pray to the LORD for you.”
units.rightText: And Samuel said, Gather all Israel to Mizpah, and I will pray for you unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: They gathered together to Mizpah, and drew water, and poured it out before the LORD, and fasted on that day, and said there, “We have sinned against the LORD.” Samuel judged the children of Israel in Mizpah.
units.rightText: And they gathered together to Mizpah, and drew water, and poured it out before Jehovah, and fasted on that day, and said there, We have sinned against Jehovah. And Samuel judged the children of Israel in Mizpah.

units.leftText: When the Philistines heard that the children of Israel were gathered together at Mizpah, the lords of the Philistines went up against Israel. When the children of Israel heard it, they were afraid of the Philistines.
units.rightText: And when the Philistines heard that the children of Israel were gathered together to Mizpah, the lords of the Philistines went up against Israel. And when the children of Israel heard it, they were afraid of the Philistines.

units.leftText: The children of Israel said to Samuel, “Don’t stop crying to the LORD our God for us, that he will save us out of the hand of the Philistines.”
units.rightText: And the children of Israel said to Samuel, Cease not to cry unto Jehovah our God for us, that he will save us out of the hand of the Philistines.

units.leftText: Samuel took a suckling lamb, and offered it for a whole burnt offering to the LORD. Samuel cried to the LORD for Israel, and the LORD answered him.
units.rightText: And Samuel took a sucking lamb, and offered it for a whole burnt-offering unto Jehovah: and Samuel cried unto Jehovah for Israel; and Jehovah answered him.

units.leftText: As Samuel was offering up the burnt offering, the Philistines came near to battle against Israel; but the LORD thundered with a great thunder on that day on the Philistines and confused them; and they were struck down before Israel.
units.rightText: And as Samuel was offering up the burnt-offering, the Philistines drew near to battle against Israel; but Jehovah thundered with a great thunder on that day upon the Philistines, and discomfited them; and they were smitten down before Israel.

units.leftText: The men of Israel went out of Mizpah and pursued the Philistines, and struck them until they came under Beth Kar.
units.rightText: And the men of Israel went out of Mizpah, and pursued the Philistines, and smote them, until they came under Beth-car.

units.leftText: Then Samuel took a stone and set it between Mizpah and Shen, and called its name Ebenezer, saying, “The LORD helped us until now.”
units.rightText: Then Samuel took a stone, and set it between Mizpah and Shen, and called the name of it Eben-ezer, saying, Hitherto hath Jehovah helped us.
leftNotes: 7:12 “Ebenezer” means “stone of help”.

units.leftText: So the Philistines were subdued, and they stopped coming within the border of Israel. The LORD’s hand was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel.
units.rightText: So the Philistines were subdued, and they came no more within the border of Israel: and the hand of Jehovah was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel.

units.leftText: The cities which the Philistines had taken from Israel were restored to Israel, from Ekron even to Gath; and Israel recovered its border out of the hand of the Philistines. There was peace between Israel and the Amorites.
units.rightText: And the cities which the Philistines had taken from Israel were restored to Israel, from Ekron even unto Gath; and the border thereof did Israel deliver out of the hand of the Philistines. And there was peace between Israel and the Amorites.

units.leftText: Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.
units.rightText: And Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.

units.leftText: He went from year to year in a circuit to Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah; and he judged Israel in all those places.
units.rightText: And he went from year to year in circuit to Beth-el, and Gilgal, and Mizpah; and he judged Israel in all those places.

units.leftText: His return was to Ramah, for his house was there, and he judged Israel there; and he built an altar to the LORD there.
units.rightText: And his return was to Ramah, for there was his house; and there he judged Israel: and he built there an altar unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: When Samuel was old, he made his sons judges over Israel.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when Samuel was old, that he made his sons judges over Israel.

units.leftText: Now the name of his firstborn was Joel, and the name of his second, Abijah. They were judges in Beersheba.
units.rightText: Now the name of his first-born was Joel; and the name of his second, Abijah: they were judges in Beer-sheba.

units.leftText: His sons didn’t walk in his ways, but turned away after dishonest gain, took bribes, and perverted justice.
units.rightText: And his sons walked not in his ways, but turned aside after lucre, and took bribes, and perverted justice.

units.leftText: Then all the elders of Israel gathered themselves together and came to Samuel to Ramah.
units.rightText: Then all the elders of Israel gathered themselves together, and came to Samuel unto Ramah;

units.leftText: They said to him, “Behold, you are old, and your sons don’t walk in your ways. Now make us a king to judge us like all the nations.”
units.rightText: and they said unto him, Behold, thou art old, and thy sons walk not in thy ways: now make us a king to judge us like all the nations.

units.leftText: But the thing displeased Samuel when they said, “Give us a king to judge us.”
units.rightText: But the thing displeased Samuel, when they said, Give us a king to judge us. And Samuel prayed unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: The LORD said to Samuel, “Listen to the voice of the people in all that they tell you; for they have not rejected you, but they have rejected me as the king over them.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Samuel, Hearken unto the voice of the people in all that they say unto thee; for they have not rejected thee, but they have rejected me, that I should not be king over them.

units.leftText: According to all the works which they have done since the day that I brought them up out of Egypt even to this day, in that they have forsaken me and served other gods, so they also do to you.
units.rightText: According to all the works which they have done since the day that I brought them up out of Egypt even unto this day, in that they have forsaken me, and served other gods, so do they also unto thee.

units.leftText: Now therefore, listen to their voice. However, you shall protest solemnly to them, and shall show them the way of the king who will reign over them.”
units.rightText: Now therefore hearken unto their voice: howbeit thou shalt protest solemnly unto them, and shalt show them the manner of the king that shall reign over them.

units.leftText: Samuel told all the LORD’s words to the people who asked him for a king.
units.rightText: And Samuel told all the words of Jehovah unto the people that asked of him a king.

units.leftText: He said, “This will be the way of the king who shall reign over you: he will take your sons and appoint them as his servants, for his chariots and to be his horsemen; and they will run before his chariots.
units.rightText: And he said, This will be the manner of the king that shall reign over you: he will take your sons, and appoint them unto him, for his chariots, and to be his horsemen; and they shall run before his chariots;

units.leftText: He will appoint them to him for captains of thousands and captains of fifties; and he will assign some to plow his ground and to reap his harvest; and to make his instruments of war and the instruments of his chariots.
units.rightText: and he will appoint them unto him for captains of thousands, and captains of fifties; and he will set some to plow his ground, and to reap his harvest, and to make his instruments of war, and the instruments of his chariots.

units.leftText: He will take your fields, your vineyards, and your olive groves, even your best, and give them to his servants.

units.rightText: And he will take the tenth of your seed, and of your vineyards, and give to his officers, and to his servants.

units.rightText: And he will take your men-servants, and your maid-servants, and your goodliest young men, and your asses, and put them to his work.

units.leftText: He will take one tenth of your flocks; and you will be his servants.
units.rightText: He will take the tenth of your flocks: and ye shall be his servants.

units.rightText: And ye shall cry out in that day because of your king whom ye shall have chosen you; and Jehovah will not answer you in that day.

units.rightText: But the people refused to hearken unto the voice of Samuel; and they said, Nay: but we will have a king over us,

units.rightText: that we also may be like all the nations, and that our king may judge us, and go out before us, and fight our battles.

units.leftText: Samuel heard all the words of the people, and he rehearsed them in the ears of the LORD.
units.rightText: And Samuel heard all the words of the people, and he rehearsed them in the ears of Jehovah.

units.leftText: The LORD said to Samuel, “Listen to their voice, and make them a king.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said to Samuel, Hearken unto their voice, and make them a king. And Samuel said unto the men of Israel, Go ye every man unto his city.

units.leftText: Now there was a man of Benjamin, whose name was Kish the son of Abiel, the son of Zeror, the son of Becorath, the son of Aphiah, the son of a Benjamite, a mighty man of valor.
units.rightText: Now there was a man of Benjamin, whose name was Kish, the son of Abiel, the son of Zeror, the son of Becorath, the son of Aphiah, the son of a Benjamite, a mighty man of valor.

units.leftText: He had a son whose name was Saul, an impressive young man; and there was not among the children of Israel a more handsome person than he. From his shoulders and upward he was taller than any of the people.
units.rightText: And he had a son, whose name was Saul, a young man and a goodly: and there was not among the children of Israel a goodlier person than he: from his shoulders and upward he was higher than any of the people.

units.leftText: The donkeys of Kish, Saul’s father, were lost. Kish said to Saul his son, “Now take one of the servants with you, and arise, go look for the donkeys.”
units.rightText: And the asses of Kish, Saul’s father, were lost. And Kish said to Saul his son, Take now one of the servants with thee, and arise, go seek the asses.

units.leftText: He passed through the hill country of Ephraim, and passed through the land of Shalishah, but they didn’t find them. Then they passed through the land of Shaalim, and they weren’t there. Then he passed through the land of the Benjamites, but they didn’t find them.
units.rightText: And he passed through the hill-country of Ephraim, and passed through the land of Shalishah, but they found them not: then they passed through the land of Shaalim, and there they were not: and he passed through the land of the Benjamites, but they found them not.

units.leftText: When they had come to the land of Zuph, Saul said to his servant who was with him, “Come! Let’s return, lest my father stop caring about the donkeys and be anxious for us.”
units.rightText: When they were come to the land of Zuph, Saul said to his servant that was with him, Come, and let us return, lest my father leave off caring for the asses, and be anxious for us.

units.leftText: The servant said to him, “Behold now, there is a man of God in this city, and he is a man who is held in honor. All that he says surely happens. Now let’s go there. Perhaps he can tell us which way to go.”
units.rightText: And he said unto him, Behold now, there is in this city a man of God, and he is a man that is held in honor; all that he saith cometh surely to pass: now let us go thither; peradventure he can tell us concerning our journey whereon we go.

units.leftText: Then Saul said to his servant, “But behold, if we go, what should we bring the man? For the bread is spent in our sacks, and there is not a present to bring to the man of God. What do we have?”
units.rightText: Then said Saul to his servant, But, behold, if we go, what shall we bring the man? for the bread is spent in our vessels, and there is not a present to bring to the man of God: what have we?

units.leftText: The servant answered Saul again and said, “Behold, I have in my hand the fourth part of a shekel of silver. I will give that to the man of God, to tell us our way.”
units.rightText: And the servant answered Saul again, and said, Behold, I have in my hand the fourth part of a shekel of silver: that will I give to the man of God, to tell us our way.

units.leftText: Then Saul said to his servant, “Well said. Come! Let’s go.” So they went to the city where the man of God was.
units.rightText: Then said Saul to his servant, Well said; come, let us go. So they went unto the city where the man of God was.

units.leftText: As they went up the ascent to the city, they found young maidens going out to draw water, and said to them, “Is the seer here?”
units.rightText: As they went up the ascent to the city, they found young maidens going out to draw water, and said unto them, Is the seer here?

units.leftText: They answered them and said, “He is. Behold, he is before you. Hurry now, for he has come today into the city; for the people have a sacrifice today in the high place.
units.rightText: And they answered them, and said, He is; behold, he is before thee: make haste now, for he is come to-day into the city; for the people have a sacrifice to-day in the high place.

units.leftText: As soon as you have come into the city, you will immediately find him before he goes up to the high place to eat; for the people will not eat until he comes, because he blesses the sacrifice. units.rightText: As soon as ye are come into the city, ye shall straightway find him, before he goeth up to the high place to eat; for the people will not eat until he come, because he doth bless the sacrifice; and afterwards they eat that are bidden. units.leftText: They went up to the city. As they came within the city, behold, Samuel came out toward them to go up to the high place.
units.rightText: And they went up to the city; and as they came within the city, behold, Samuel came out toward them, to go up to the high place.

units.leftText: Now the LORD had revealed to Samuel a day before Saul came, saying,
units.rightText: Now Jehovah had revealed unto Samuel a day before Saul came, saying,

units.leftText: “Tomorrow about this time I will send you a man out of the land of Benjamin, and you shall anoint him to be prince over my people Israel. He will save my people out of the hand of the Philistines; for I have looked upon my people, because their cry has come to me.”
units.rightText: To-morrow about this time I will send thee a man out of the land of Benjamin, and thou shalt anoint him to be prince over my people Israel; and he shall save my people out of the hand of the Philistines: for I have looked upon my people, because their cry is come unto me.

units.leftText: When Samuel saw Saul, the LORD said to him, “Behold, the man of whom I spoke to you! He will have authority over my people.”
units.rightText: And when Samuel saw Saul, Jehovah said unto him, Behold, the man of whom I spake to thee! this same shall have authority over my people.

units.leftText: Then Saul approached Samuel in the gateway, and said, “Please tell me where the seer’s house is.”
units.rightText: Then Saul drew near to Samuel in the gate, and said, Tell me, I pray thee, where the seer’s house is.

units.leftText: Samuel answered Saul and said, “I am the seer. Go up before me to the high place, for you are to eat with me today. In the morning I will let you go and will tell you all that is in your heart.
units.rightText: And Samuel answered Saul, and said, I am the seer; go up before me unto the high place, for ye shall eat with me to-day: and in the morning I will let thee go, and will tell thee all that is in thy heart.

units.leftText: As for your donkeys who were lost three days ago, don’t set your mind on them, for they have been found. For whom does all Israel desire? Is it not you and all your father’s house?”
units.rightText: And as for thine asses that were lost three days ago, set not thy mind on them; for they are found. And for whom is all that is desirable in Israel? Is it not for thee, and for all thy father’s house?

units.leftText: Saul answered, “Am I not a Benjamite, of the smallest of the tribes of Israel? And my family the least of all the families of the tribe of Benjamin? Why then do you speak to me like this?”
units.rightText: And Saul answered and said, Am not I a Benjamite, of the smallest of the tribes of Israel? and my family the least of all the families of the tribe of Benjamin? wherefore then speakest thou to me after this manner?

units.leftText: Samuel took Saul and his servant and brought them into the guest room, and made them sit in the best place among those who were invited, who were about thirty persons.
units.rightText: And Samuel took Saul and his servant, and brought them into the guest-chamber, and made them sit in the chiefest place among them that were bidden, who were about thirty persons.

units.leftText: Samuel said to the cook, “Bring the portion which I gave you, of which I said to you, ‘Set it aside.’”
units.rightText: And Samuel said unto the cook, Bring the portion which I gave thee, of which I said unto thee, Set it by thee.

units.leftText: The cook took up the thigh, and that which was on it, and set it before Saul. Samuel said, “Behold, that which has been reserved! Set it before yourself and eat; because it has been kept for you for the appointed time, for I said, ‘I have invited the people.’” So Saul ate with Samuel that day.
units.rightText: And the cook took up the thigh, and that which was upon it, and set it before Saul. And Samuel said, Behold, that which hath been reserved! set it before thee and eat; because unto the appointed time hath it been kept for thee, for I said, I have invited the people. So Saul did eat with Samuel that day.

units.leftText: When they had come down from the high place into the city, he talked with Saul on the housetop.
units.rightText: And when they were come down from the high place into the city, he communed with Saul upon the housetop.

units.leftText: They arose early; and about daybreak, Samuel called to Saul on the housetop, saying, “Get up, that I may send you away.” Saul arose, and they both went outside, he and Samuel, together.
units.rightText: And they arose early: and it came to pass about the spring of the day, that Samuel called to Saul on the housetop, saying, Up, that I may send thee away. And Saul arose, and they went out both of them, he and Samuel, abroad.

units.leftText: As they were going down at the end of the city, Samuel said to Saul, “Tell the servant to go on ahead of us.” He went ahead, then Samuel said, “But stand still first, that I may cause you to hear God’s message.”
units.rightText: As they were going down at the end of the city, Samuel said to Saul, Bid the servant pass on before us (and he passed on), but stand thou still first, that I may cause thee to hear the word of God.

units.leftText: Then Samuel took the vial of oil and poured it on his head, then kissed him and said, “Hasn’t the LORD anointed you to be prince over his inheritance?
units.rightText: Then Samuel took the vial of oil, and poured it upon his head, and kissed him, and said, Is it not that Jehovah hath anointed thee to be prince over his inheritance?

units.leftText: When you have departed from me today, then you will find two men by Rachel’s tomb, on the border of Benjamin at Zelzah.
