units.rightText: When thou art departed from me to-day, then thou shalt find two men by Rachel’s sepulchre, in the border of Benjamin at Zelzah; and they will say unto thee, The asses which thou wentest to seek are found; and, lo, thy father hath left off caring for the asses, and is anxious for you, saying, What shall I do for my son?

units.leftText: “Then you will go on forward from there, and you will come to the oak of Tabor. Three men will meet you there going up to God to Bethel: one carrying three young goats, and another carrying three loaves of bread, and another carrying a container of wine.
units.rightText: Then shalt thou go on forward from thence, and thou shalt come to the oak of Tabor; and there shall meet thee there three men going up to God to Beth-el, one carrying three kids, and another carrying three loaves of bread, and another carrying a bottle of wine:

units.leftText: They will greet you and give you two loaves of bread, which you shall receive from their hand.
units.rightText: and they will salute thee, and give thee two loaves of bread, which thou shalt receive of their hand.

units.leftText: “After that you will come to the hill of God, where the garrison of the Philistines is; and it will happen, when you have come there to the city, that you will meet a band of prophets coming down from the high place with a lute, a tambourine, a pipe, and a harp before them; and they will be prophesying.
units.rightText: After that thou shalt come to the hill of God, where is the garrison of the Philistines: and it shall come to pass, when thou art come thither to the city, that thou shalt meet a band of prophets coming down from the high place with a psaltery, and a timbrel, and a pipe, and a harp, before them; and they will be prophesying:

units.leftText: Then the LORD’s Spirit will come mightily on you, then you will prophesy with them and will be turned into another man.
units.rightText: and the Spirit of Jehovah will come mightily upon thee, and thou shalt prophesy with them, and shalt be turned into another man.

units.leftText: Let it be, when these signs have come to you, that you do what is appropriate for the occasion; for God is with you.
units.rightText: And let it be, when these signs are come unto thee, that thou do as occasion shall serve thee; for God is with thee.

units.leftText: “Go down ahead of me to Gilgal; and behold, I will come down to you to offer burnt offerings and to sacrifice sacrifices of peace offerings. Wait seven days, until I come to you and show you what you are to do.”
units.rightText: And thou shalt go down before me to Gilgal; and, behold, I will come down unto thee, to offer burnt-offerings, and to sacrifice sacrifices of peace-offerings: seven days shalt thou tarry, till I come unto thee, and show thee what thou shalt do.

units.leftText: It was so, that when he had turned his back to go from Samuel, God gave him another heart; and all those signs happened that day.
units.rightText: And it was so, that, when he had turned his back to go from Samuel, God gave him another heart: and all those signs came to pass that day.

units.leftText: When they came there to the hill, behold, a band of prophets met him; and the Spirit of God came mightily on him, and he prophesied among them.
units.rightText: And when they came thither to the hill, behold, a band of prophets met him; and the Spirit of God came mightily upon him, and he prophesied among them.

units.leftText: When all who knew him before saw that, behold, he prophesied with the prophets, then the people said to one another, “What is this that has come to the son of Kish? Is Saul also among the prophets?”
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when all that knew him beforetime saw that, behold, he prophesied with the prophets, then the people said one to another, What is this that is come unto the son of Kish? Is Saul also among the prophets?

units.leftText: One from the same place answered, “Who is their father?” Therefore it became a proverb, “Is Saul also among the prophets?”
units.rightText: And one of the same place answered and said, And who is their father? Therefore it became a proverb, Is Saul also among the prophets?

units.leftText: When he had finished prophesying, he came to the high place.
units.rightText: And when he had made an end of prophesying, he came to the high place.

units.leftText: Saul’s uncle said to him and to his servant, “Where did you go?”
units.rightText: And Saul’s uncle said unto him and to his servant, Whither went ye? And he said, To seek the asses; and when we saw that they were not found, we came to Samuel.

units.leftText: Saul’s uncle said, “Please tell me what Samuel said to you.”
units.rightText: And Saul’s uncle said, Tell me, I pray thee, what Samuel said unto you.

units.leftText: Saul said to his uncle, “He told us plainly that the donkeys were found.” But concerning the matter of the kingdom, of which Samuel spoke, he didn’t tell him.
units.rightText: And Saul said unto his uncle, He told us plainly that the asses were found. But concerning the matter of the kingdom, whereof Samuel spake, he told him not.

units.leftText: Samuel called the people together to the LORD to Mizpah;
units.rightText: And Samuel called the people together unto Jehovah to Mizpah;

units.leftText: and he said to the children of Israel, “The LORD, the God of Israel, says ‘I brought Israel up out of Egypt and I delivered you out of the hand of the Egyptians, and out of the hand of all the kingdoms that oppressed you.’
units.rightText: and he said unto the children of Israel, Thus saith Jehovah, the God of Israel, I brought up Israel out of Egypt, and I delivered you out of the hand of the Egyptians, and out of the hand of all the kingdoms that oppressed you:

units.leftText: But you have today rejected your God, who himself saves you out of all your calamities and your distresses; and you have said to him, ‘No! Set a king over us!’ Now therefore present yourselves before the LORD by your tribes and by your thousands.”
units.rightText: but ye have this day rejected your God, who himself saveth you out of all your calamities and your distresses; and ye have said unto him, Nay, but set a king over us. Now therefore present yourselves before Jehovah by your tribes, and by your thousands.

units.leftText: So Samuel brought all the tribes of Israel near, and the tribe of Benjamin was chosen.
units.rightText: So Samuel brought all the tribes of Israel near, and the tribe of Benjamin was taken.

units.leftText: He brought the tribe of Benjamin near by their families and the family of the Matrites was chosen. Then Saul the son of Kish was chosen; but when they looked for him, he could not be found.
units.rightText: And he brought the tribe of Benjamin near by their families; and the family of the Matrites was taken; and Saul the son of Kish was taken: but when they sought him, he could not be found.

units.leftText: Therefore they asked of the LORD further, “Is there yet a man to come here?”
units.rightText: Therefore they asked of Jehovah further, Is there yet a man to come hither? And Jehovah answered, Behold, he hath hid himself among the baggage.

units.leftText: They ran and got him there. When he stood among the people, he was higher than any of the people from his shoulders and upward.
units.rightText: And they ran and fetched him thence; and when he stood among the people, he was higher than any of the people from his shoulders and upward.

units.leftText: Samuel said to all the people, “Do you see him whom the LORD has chosen, that there is no one like him among all the people?”
units.rightText: And Samuel said to all the people, See ye him whom Jehovah hath chosen, that there is none like him among all the people? And all the people shouted, and said, Long live the king.

units.leftText: Then Samuel told the people the regulations of the kingdom, and wrote it in a book and laid it up before the LORD. Samuel sent all the people away, every man to his house.
units.rightText: Then Samuel told the people the manner of the kingdom, and wrote it in a book, and laid it up before Jehovah. And Samuel sent all the people away, every man to his house.

units.leftText: Saul also went to his house in Gibeah; and the army went with him, whose hearts God had touched.
units.rightText: And Saul also went to his house to Gibeah; and there went with him the host, whose hearts God had touched.

units.leftText: But certain worthless fellows said, “How could this man save us?” They despised him, and brought him no tribute. But he held his peace.
units.rightText: But certain worthless fellows said, How shall this man save us? And they despised him, and brought him no present. But he held his peace.

units.leftText: Then Nahash the Ammonite came up and encamped against Jabesh Gilead; and all the men of Jabesh said to Nahash, “Make a covenant with us, and we will serve you.”
units.rightText: Then Nahash the Ammonite came up, and encamped against Jabesh-gilead: and all the men of Jabesh said unto Nahash, Make a covenant with us, and we will serve thee.

units.leftText: Nahash the Ammonite said to them, “On this condition I will make it with you, that all your right eyes be gouged out. I will make this dishonor all Israel.”
units.rightText: And Nahash the Ammonite said unto them, On this condition will I make it with you, that all your right eyes be put out; and I will lay it for a reproach upon all Israel.

units.leftText: The elders of Jabesh said to him, “Give us seven days, that we may send messengers to all the borders of Israel; and then, if there is no one to save us, we will come out to you.”
units.rightText: And the elders of Jabesh said unto him, Give us seven days’ respite, that we may send messengers unto all the borders of Israel; and then, if there be none to save us, we will come out to thee.

units.leftText: Then the messengers came to Gibeah of Saul, and spoke these words in the ears of the people, then all the people lifted up their voice and wept.
units.rightText: Then came the messengers to Gibeah of Saul, and spake these words in the ears of the people: and all the people lifted up their voice, and wept.

units.leftText: Behold, Saul came following the oxen out of the field; and Saul said, “What ails the people that they weep?” They told him the words of the men of Jabesh.
units.rightText: And, behold, Saul came following the oxen out of the field; and Saul said, What aileth the people that they weep? And they told him the words of the men of Jabesh.

units.leftText: God’s Spirit came mightily on Saul when he heard those words, and his anger burned hot.
units.rightText: And the Spirit of God came mightily upon Saul when he heard those words, and his anger was kindled greatly.

units.leftText: He took a yoke of oxen and cut them in pieces, then sent them throughout all the borders of Israel by the hand of messengers, saying, “Whoever doesn’t come out after Saul and after Samuel, so shall it be done to his oxen.” The dread of the LORD fell on the people, and they came out as one man.
units.rightText: And he took a yoke of oxen, and cut them in pieces, and sent them throughout all the borders of Israel by the hand of messengers, saying, Whosoever cometh not forth after Saul and after Samuel, so shall it be done unto his oxen. And the dread of Jehovah fell on the people, and they came out as one man.

units.leftText: He counted them in Bezek; and the children of Israel were three hundred thousand, and the men of Judah thirty thousand.
units.rightText: And he numbered them in Bezek; and the children of Israel were three hundred thousand, and the men of Judah thirty thousand.

units.leftText: They said to the messengers who came, “Tell the men of Jabesh Gilead, ‘Tomorrow, by the time the sun is hot, you will be rescued.’” The messengers came and told the men of Jabesh; and they were glad.
units.rightText: And they said unto the messengers that came, Thus shall ye say unto the men of Jabesh-gilead, To-morrow, by the time the sun is hot, ye shall have deliverance. And the messengers came and told the men of Jabesh; and they were glad.

units.leftText: Therefore the men of Jabesh said, “Tomorrow we will come out to you, and you shall do with us all that seems good to you.”
units.rightText: Therefore the men of Jabesh said, To-morrow we will come out unto you, and ye shall do with us all that seemeth good unto you.

units.leftText: On the next day, Saul put the people in three companies; and they came into the middle of the camp in the morning watch, and struck the Ammonites until the heat of the day. Those who remained were scattered, so that no two of them were left together.
units.rightText: And it was so on the morrow, that Saul put the people in three companies; and they came into the midst of the camp in the morning watch, and smote the Ammonites until the heat of the day: and it came to pass, that they that remained were scattered, so that not two of them were left together.

units.leftText: The people said to Samuel, “Who is he who said, ‘Shall Saul reign over us?’ Bring those men, that we may put them to death!”
units.rightText: And the people said unto Samuel, Who is he that said, Shall Saul reign over us? bring the men, that we may put them to death.

units.leftText: Saul said, “No man shall be put to death today; for today the LORD has rescued Israel.”
units.rightText: And Saul said, There shall not a man be put to death this day; for to-day Jehovah hath wrought deliverance in Israel.

units.leftText: Then Samuel said to the people, “Come! Let’s go to Gilgal, and renew the kingdom there.”
units.rightText: Then said Samuel to the people, Come, and let us go to Gilgal, and renew the kingdom there.

units.leftText: All the people went to Gilgal; and there they made Saul king before the LORD in Gilgal. There they offered sacrifices of peace offerings before the LORD; and there Saul and all the men of Israel rejoiced greatly.
units.rightText: And all the people went to Gilgal; and there they made Saul king before Jehovah in Gilgal; and there they offered sacrifices of peace-offerings before Jehovah; and there Saul and all the men of Israel rejoiced greatly.

units.leftText: Samuel said to all Israel, “Behold, I have listened to your voice in all that you said to me, and have made a king over you.
units.rightText: And Samuel said unto all Israel, Behold, I have hearkened unto your voice in all that ye said unto me, and have made a king over you.

units.leftText: Now, behold, the king walks before you. I am old and gray-headed. Behold, my sons are with you. I have walked before you from my youth to this day.
units.rightText: And now, behold, the king walketh before you; and I am old and grayheaded; and, behold, my sons are with you: and I have walked before you from my youth unto this day.

units.leftText: Here I am. Witness against me before the LORD and before his anointed. Whose ox have I taken? Whose donkey have I taken? Whom have I defrauded? Whom have I oppressed? Of whose hand have I taken a bribe to make me blind my eyes? I will restore it to you.”
units.rightText: Here I am: witness against me before Jehovah, and before his anointed: whose ox have I taken? or whose ass have I taken? or whom have I defrauded? whom have I oppressed? or of whose hand have I taken a ransom to blind mine eyes therewith? and I will restore it you.

units.leftText: They said, “You have not defrauded us, nor oppressed us, neither have you taken anything from anyone’s hand.”
units.rightText: And they said, Thou hast not defrauded us, nor oppressed us, neither hast thou taken aught of any man’s hand.

units.leftText: He said to them, “The LORD is witness against you, and his anointed is witness today, that you have not found anything in my hand.”
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Jehovah is witness against you, and his anointed is witness this day, that ye have not found aught in my hand. And they said, He is witness.

units.leftText: Samuel said to the people, “It is the LORD who appointed Moses and Aaron, and that brought your fathers up out of the land of Egypt.
units.rightText: And Samuel said unto the people, It is Jehovah that appointed Moses and Aaron, and that brought your fathers up out of the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: Now therefore stand still, that I may plead with you before the LORD concerning all the righteous acts of the LORD, which he did to you and to your fathers.
units.rightText: Now therefore stand still, that I may plead with you before Jehovah concerning all the righteous acts of Jehovah, which he did to you and to your fathers.

units.leftText: “When Jacob had come into Egypt, and your fathers cried to the LORD, then the LORD sent Moses and Aaron, who brought your fathers out of Egypt, and made them to dwell in this place.
units.rightText: When Jacob was come into Egypt, and your fathers cried unto Jehovah, then Jehovah sent Moses and Aaron, who brought forth your fathers out of Egypt, and made them to dwell in this place.

units.leftText: But they forgot the LORD their God; and he sold them into the hand of Sisera, captain of the army of Hazor, and into the hand of the Philistines, and into the hand of the king of Moab; and they fought against them.
units.rightText: But they forgat Jehovah their God; and he sold them into the hand of Sisera, captain of the host of Hazor, and into the hand of the Philistines, and into the hand of the king of Moab; and they fought against them.

units.leftText: They cried to the LORD, and said, ‘We have sinned, because we have forsaken the LORD and have served the Baals and the Ashtaroth; but now deliver us out of the hand of our enemies, and we will serve you.’
units.rightText: And they cried unto Jehovah, and said, We have sinned, because we have forsaken Jehovah, and have served the Baalim and the Ashtaroth: but now deliver us out of the hand of our enemies, and we will serve thee.

units.leftText: The LORD sent Jerubbaal, Bedan, Jephthah, and Samuel, and delivered you out of the hand of your enemies on every side; and you lived in safety.
units.rightText: And Jehovah sent Jerubbaal, and Bedan, and Jephthah, and Samuel, and delivered you out of the hand of your enemies on every side; and ye dwelt in safety.

units.leftText: “When you saw that Nahash the king of the children of Ammon came against you, you said to me, ‘No, but a king shall reign over us,’ when the LORD your God was your king.
units.rightText: And when ye saw that Nahash the king of the children of Ammon came against you, ye said unto me, Nay, but a king shall reign over us; when Jehovah your God was your king.

units.leftText: Now therefore see the king whom you have chosen and whom you have asked for. Behold, the LORD has set a king over you.
units.rightText: Now therefore behold the king whom ye have chosen, and whom ye have asked for: and, behold, Jehovah hath set a king over you.

units.leftText: If you will fear the LORD, and serve him, and listen to his voice, and not rebel against the commandment of the LORD, then both you and also the king who reigns over you are followers of the LORD your God.
units.rightText: If ye will fear Jehovah, and serve him, and hearken unto his voice, and not rebel against the commandment of Jehovah, and both ye and also the king that reigneth over you be followers of Jehovah your God, well:

units.rightText: but if ye will not hearken unto the voice of Jehovah, but rebel against the commandment of Jehovah, then will the hand of Jehovah be against you, as it was against your fathers.

units.leftText: “Now therefore stand still and see this great thing, which the LORD will do before your eyes.

units.leftText: Isn’t it wheat harvest today? I will call to the LORD, that he may send thunder and rain; and you will know and see that your wickedness is great, which you have done in the LORD’s sight, in asking for a king.”
units.rightText: Is it not wheat harvest to-day? I will call unto Jehovah, that he may send thunder and rain; and ye shall know and see that your wickedness is great, which ye have done in the sight of Jehovah, in asking you a king.

units.rightText: So Samuel called unto Jehovah; and Jehovah sent thunder and rain that day: and all the people greatly feared Jehovah and Samuel.

units.leftText: All the people said to Samuel, “Pray for your servants to the LORD your God, that we not die; for we have added to all our sins this evil, to ask for a king.”
units.rightText: And all the people said unto Samuel, Pray for thy servants unto Jehovah thy God, that we die not; for we have added unto all our sins this evil, to ask us a king.

units.rightText: And Samuel said unto the people, Fear not: ye have indeed done all this evil; yet turn not aside from following Jehovah, but serve Jehovah with all your heart:

units.leftText: Saul chose for himself three thousand men of Israel, of which two thousand were with Saul in Michmash and in the Mount of Bethel, and one thousand were with Jonathan in Gibeah of Benjamin. He sent the rest of the people to their own tents.
units.rightText: Saul chose him three thousand men of Israel, whereof two thousand were with Saul in Michmash and in the mount of Beth-el, and a thousand were with Jonathan in Gibeah of Benjamin: and the rest of the people he sent every man to his tent.

units.rightText: And he tarried seven days, according to the set time that Samuel had appointed: but Samuel came not to Gilgal; and the people were scattered from him.

units.leftText: Saul said, “Bring the burnt offering to me here, and the peace offerings.” He offered the burnt offering.
units.rightText: And Saul said, Bring hither the burnt-offering to me, and the peace-offerings. And he offered the burnt-offering.

units.leftText: Samuel said, “What have you done?”
units.rightText: And Samuel said, What hast thou done? And Saul said, Because I saw that the people were scattered from me, and that thou camest not within the days appointed, and that the Philistines assembled themselves together at Michmash;

units.rightText: And Samuel said to Saul, Thou hast done foolishly; thou hast not kept the commandment of Jehovah thy God, which he commanded thee: for now would Jehovah have established thy kingdom upon Israel for ever.

units.leftText: But now your kingdom will not continue. The LORD has sought for himself a man after his own heart, and the LORD has appointed him to be prince over his people, because you have not kept that which the LORD commanded you.”
units.rightText: But now thy kingdom shall not continue: Jehovah hath sought him a man after his own heart, and Jehovah hath appointed him to be prince over his people, because thou hast not kept that which Jehovah commanded thee.

units.leftText: Samuel arose, and went from Gilgal to Gibeah of Benjamin. Saul counted the people who were present with him, about six hundred men.
units.rightText: And Samuel arose, and gat him up from Gilgal unto Gibeah of Benjamin.

units.leftText: Saul, and Jonathan his son, and the people who were present with them, stayed in Geba of Benjamin; but the Philistines encamped in Michmash.
units.rightText: And Saul, and Jonathan his son, and the people that were present with them, abode in Geba of Benjamin: but the Philistines encamped in Michmash.

units.rightText: and another company turned the way to Beth-horon; and another company turned the way of the border that looketh down upon the valley of Zeboim toward the wilderness.

units.rightText: And the garrison of the Philistines went out unto the pass of Michmash.

units.leftText: Now it happened on a day that Jonathan the son of Saul said to the young man who bore his armor, “Come! Let’s go over to the Philistines’ garrison that is on the other side.” But he didn’t tell his father.
units.rightText: Now it fell upon a day, that Jonathan the son of Saul said unto the young man that bare his armor, Come, and let us go over to the Philistines’ garrison, that is on yonder side. But he told not his father.

units.leftText: Between the passes, by which Jonathan sought to go over to the Philistines’ garrison, there was a rocky crag on the one side and a rocky crag on the other side; and the name of the one was Bozez, and the name of the other Seneh.

units.rightText: The one crag rose up on the north in front of Michmash, and the other on the south in front of Geba.

units.leftText: Jonathan said to the young man who bore his armor, “Come! Let’s go over to the garrison of these uncircumcised. It may be that the LORD will work for us, for there is no restraint on the LORD to save by many or by few.”
units.rightText: And Jonathan said to the young man that bare his armor, Come, and let us go over unto the garrison of these uncircumcised: it may be that Jehovah will work for us; for there is no restraint to Jehovah to save by many or by few.

units.leftText: His armor bearer said to him, “Do all that is in your heart. Go, and behold, I am with you according to your heart.”
units.rightText: And his armorbearer said unto him, Do all that is in thy heart: turn thee, behold, I am with thee according to thy heart.

units.leftText: Then Jonathan said, “Behold, we will pass over to the men, and we will reveal ourselves to them.
units.rightText: Then said Jonathan, Behold, we will pass over unto the men, and we will disclose ourselves unto them.

units.leftText: If they say this to us, ‘Wait until we come to you!’ then we will stand still in our place and will not go up to them.
units.rightText: If they say thus unto us, Tarry until we come to you; then we will stand still in our place, and will not go up unto them.

units.leftText: But if they say this, ‘Come up to us!’ then we will go up, for the LORD has delivered them into our hand. This shall be the sign to us.”
units.rightText: But if they say thus, Come up unto us; then we will go up; for Jehovah hath delivered them into our hand: and this shall be the sign unto us.

units.leftText: Both of them revealed themselves to the garrison of the Philistines; and the Philistines said, “Behold, the Hebrews are coming out of the holes where they had hidden themselves!”
units.rightText: And both of them disclosed themselves unto the garrison of the Philistines: and the Philistines said, Behold, the Hebrews come forth out of the holes where they had hid themselves.

units.leftText: The men of the garrison answered Jonathan and his armor bearer, and said, “Come up to us, and we will show you something!”
units.rightText: And the men of the garrison answered Jonathan and his armorbearer, and said, Come up to us, and we will show you a thing. And Jonathan said unto his armorbearer, Come up after me; for Jehovah hath delivered them into the hand of Israel.

units.leftText: Jonathan climbed up on his hands and on his feet, and his armor bearer after him, and they fell before Jonathan; and his armor bearer killed them after him.
units.rightText: And Jonathan climbed up upon his hands and upon his feet, and his armorbearer after him: and they fell before Jonathan; and his armorbearer slew them after him.

units.leftText: That first slaughter, which Jonathan and his armor bearer made, was about twenty men, within as it were half a furrow’s length in an acre of land.
units.rightText: And that first slaughter, which Jonathan and his armorbearer made, was about twenty men, within as it were half a furrow’s length in an acre of land.

units.leftText: There was a trembling in the camp, in the field, and among all the people; the garrison and the raiders also trembled; and the earth quaked, so there was an exceedingly great trembling.
units.rightText: And there was a trembling in the camp, in the field, and among all the people; the garrison, and the spoilers, they also trembled; and the earth quaked: so there was an exceeding great trembling.

units.leftText: The watchmen of Saul in Gibeah of Benjamin looked; and behold, the multitude melted away and scattered.
units.rightText: And the watchmen of Saul in Gibeah of Benjamin looked; and, behold, the multitude melted away, and they went hither and thither.

units.leftText: Then Saul said to the people who were with him, “Count now, and see who is missing from us.” When they had counted, behold, Jonathan and his armor bearer were not there.
units.rightText: Then said Saul unto the people that were with him, Number now, and see who is gone from us. And when they had numbered, behold, Jonathan and his armorbearer were not there.

units.leftText: Saul said to Ahijah, “Bring God’s ark here.” For God’s ark was with the children of Israel at that time.
units.rightText: And Saul said unto Ahijah, Bring hither the ark of God. For the ark of God was there at that time with the children of Israel.

units.leftText: While Saul talked to the priest, the tumult that was in the camp of the Philistines went on and increased; and Saul said to the priest, “Withdraw your hand!”
units.rightText: And it came to pass, while Saul talked unto the priest, that the tumult that was in the camp of the Philistines went on and increased: and Saul said unto the priest, Withdraw thy hand.

units.leftText: Saul and all the people who were with him were gathered together, and came to the battle; and behold, they were all striking each other with their swords in very great confusion.
units.rightText: And Saul and all the people that were with him were gathered together, and came to the battle: and, behold, every man’s sword was against his fellow, and there was a very great discomfiture.

units.leftText: Now the Hebrews who were with the Philistines before and who went up with them into the camp from all around, even they also turned to be with the Israelites who were with Saul and Jonathan.
units.rightText: Now the Hebrews that were with the Philistines as beforetime, and that went up with them into the camp, from the country round about, even they also turned to be with the Israelites that were with Saul and Jonathan.

units.leftText: Likewise all the men of Israel who had hidden themselves in the hill country of Ephraim, when they heard that the Philistines fled, even they also followed hard after them in the battle.
units.rightText: Likewise all the men of Israel that had hid themselves in the hill-country of Ephraim, when they heard that the Philistines fled, even they also followed hard after them in the battle.

units.leftText: So the LORD saved Israel that day; and the battle passed over by Beth Aven.
units.rightText: So Jehovah saved Israel that day: and the battle passed over by Beth-aven.

units.leftText: The men of Israel were distressed that day; for Saul had adjured the people, saying, “Cursed is the man who eats any food until it is evening, and I am avenged of my enemies.” So none of the people tasted food.
units.rightText: And the men of Israel were distressed that day; for Saul had adjured the people, saying, Cursed be the man that eateth any food until it be evening, and I be avenged on mine enemies. So none of the people tasted food.

units.leftText: All the people came into the forest; and there was honey on the ground.
units.rightText: And all the people came into the forest; and there was honey upon the ground.

units.leftText: When the people had come to the forest, behold, honey was dripping, but no one put his hand to his mouth, for the people feared the oath.
units.rightText: And when the people were come unto the forest, behold, the honey dropped: but no man put his hand to his mouth; for the people feared the oath.

units.leftText: But Jonathan didn’t hear when his father commanded the people with the oath. Therefore he put out the end of the rod that was in his hand and dipped it in the honeycomb, and put his hand to his mouth; and his eyes brightened.
units.rightText: But Jonathan heard not when his father charged the people with the oath: wherefore he put forth the end of the rod that was in his hand, and dipped it in the honeycomb, and put his hand to his mouth; and his eyes were enlightened.

units.leftText: Then one of the people answered, and said, “Your father directly commanded the people with an oath, saying, ‘Cursed is the man who eats food today.’” So the people were faint.
units.rightText: Then answered one of the people, and said, Thy father straitly charged the people with an oath, saying, Cursed be the man that eateth food this day. And the people were faint.

units.leftText: Then Jonathan said, “My father has troubled the land. Please look how my eyes have brightened because I tasted a little of this honey.
units.rightText: Then said Jonathan, My father hath troubled the land: see, I pray you, how mine eyes have been enlightened, because I tasted a little of this honey.

units.leftText: How much more, if perhaps the people had eaten freely today of the plunder of their enemies which they found? For now there has been no great slaughter among the Philistines.”
units.rightText: How much more, if haply the people had eaten freely to-day of the spoil of their enemies which they found? for now hath there been no great slaughter among the Philistines.

units.leftText: They struck the Philistines that day from Michmash to Aijalon. The people were very faint;
units.rightText: And they smote of the Philistines that day from Michmash to Aijalon. And the people were very faint;

units.leftText: and the people pounced on the plunder, and took sheep, cattle, and calves, and killed them on the ground; and the people ate them with the blood.
units.rightText: and the people flew upon the spoil, and took sheep, and oxen, and calves, and slew them on the ground; and the people did eat them with the blood.

units.leftText: Then they told Saul, saying, “Behold, the people are sinning against the LORD, in that they eat meat with the blood.”
units.rightText: Then they told Saul, saying, Behold, the people sin against Jehovah, in that they eat with the blood. And he said, Ye have dealt treacherously: roll a great stone unto me this day.

units.leftText: Saul said, “Disperse yourselves among the people, and tell them, ‘Every man bring me here his ox, and every man his sheep, and kill them here, and eat; and don’t sin against the LORD in eating meat with the blood.’” All the people brought every man his ox with him that night, and killed them there.
units.rightText: And Saul said, Disperse yourselves among the people, and say unto them, Bring me hither every man his ox, and every man his sheep, and slay them here, and eat; and sin not against Jehovah in eating with the blood. And all the people brought every man his ox with him that night, and slew them there.

units.leftText: Saul built an altar to the LORD. This was the first altar that he built to the LORD.
units.rightText: And Saul built an altar unto Jehovah: the same was the first altar that he built unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: Saul said, “Let’s go down after the Philistines by night, and take plunder among them until the morning light. Let’s not leave a man of them.”
units.rightText: And Saul said, Let us go down after the Philistines by night, and take spoil among them until the morning light, and let us not leave a man of them. And they said, Do whatsoever seemeth good unto thee. Then said the priest, Let us draw near hither unto God.

units.leftText: Saul asked counsel of God: “Shall I go down after the Philistines? Will you deliver them into the hand of Israel?” But he didn’t answer him that day.
units.rightText: And Saul asked counsel of God, Shall I go down after the Philistines? wilt thou deliver them into the hand of Israel? But he answered him not that day.

units.leftText: Saul said, “Draw near here, all you chiefs of the people, and know and see in whom this sin has been today.
units.rightText: And Saul said, Draw nigh hither, all ye chiefs of the people; and know and see wherein this sin hath been this day.

units.leftText: For as the LORD lives, who saves Israel, though it is in Jonathan my son, he shall surely die.” But there was not a man among all the people who answered him.
units.rightText: For, as Jehovah liveth, who saveth Israel, though it be in Jonathan my son, he shall surely die. But there was not a man among all the people that answered him.

units.leftText: Then he said to all Israel, “You be on one side, and I and Jonathan my son will be on the other side.”
units.rightText: Then said he unto all Israel, Be ye on one side, and I and Jonathan my son will be on the other side. And the people said unto Saul, Do what seemeth good unto thee.

units.leftText: Therefore Saul said to the LORD, the God of Israel, “Show the right.”
units.rightText: Therefore Saul said unto Jehovah, the God of Israel, Show the right. And Jonathan and Saul were taken by lot; but the people escaped.

units.leftText: Saul said, “Cast lots between me and Jonathan my son.”
units.rightText: And Saul said, Cast lots between me and Jonathan my son. And Jonathan was taken.

units.leftText: Then Saul said to Jonathan, “Tell me what you have done!”
units.rightText: Then Saul said to Jonathan, Tell me what thou hast done. And Jonathan told him, and said, I did certainly taste a little honey with the end of the rod that was in my hand; and, lo, I must die.

units.leftText: Saul said, “God do so and more also; for you shall surely die, Jonathan.”
units.rightText: And Saul said, God do so and more also; for thou shalt surely die, Jonathan.

units.leftText: The people said to Saul, “Shall Jonathan die, who has worked this great salvation in Israel? Far from it! As the LORD lives, there shall not one hair of his head fall to the ground, for he has worked with God today!” So the people rescued Jonathan, so he didn’t die.
units.rightText: And the people said unto Saul, Shall Jonathan die, who hath wrought this great salvation in Israel? Far from it: as Jehovah liveth, there shall not one hair of his head fall to the ground; for he hath wrought with God this day. So the people rescued Jonathan, that he died not.

units.leftText: Then Saul went up from following the Philistines; and the Philistines went to their own place.
units.rightText: Then Saul went up from following the Philistines; and the Philistines went to their own place.

units.leftText: Now when Saul had taken the kingdom over Israel, he fought against all his enemies on every side: against Moab, and against the children of Ammon, and against Edom, and against the kings of Zobah, and against the Philistines. Wherever he turned himself, he defeated them.

units.leftText: Samuel rose early to meet Saul in the morning; and Samuel was told, saying, “Saul came to Carmel, and behold, he set up a monument for himself, turned, passed on, and went down to Gilgal.”
units.rightText: And Samuel rose early to meet Saul in the morning; and it was told Samuel, saying, Saul came to Carmel, and, behold, he set him up a monument, and turned, and passed on, and went down to Gilgal.

units.leftText: Samuel came to Saul; and Saul said to him, “You are blessed by the LORD! I have performed the commandment of the LORD.”
units.rightText: And Samuel came to Saul; and Saul said unto him, Blessed be thou of Jehovah: I have performed the commandment of Jehovah.

units.leftText: Samuel said, “Then what does this bleating of the sheep in my ears and the lowing of the cattle which I hear mean?”
units.rightText: And Samuel said, What meaneth then this bleating of the sheep in mine ears, and the lowing of the oxen which I hear?

units.leftText: Saul said, “They have brought them from the Amalekites; for the people spared the best of the sheep and of the cattle, to sacrifice to the LORD your God. We have utterly destroyed the rest.”
units.rightText: And Saul said, They have brought them from the Amalekites: for the people spared the best of the sheep and of the oxen, to sacrifice unto Jehovah thy God; and the rest we have utterly destroyed.

units.leftText: Then Samuel said to Saul, “Stay, and I will tell you what the LORD said to me last night.”
units.rightText: Then Samuel said unto Saul, Stay, and I will tell thee what Jehovah hath said to me this night. And he said unto him, Say on.

units.leftText: Samuel said, “Though you were little in your own sight, weren’t you made the head of the tribes of Israel? The LORD anointed you king over Israel;
units.rightText: And Samuel said, Though thou wast little in thine own sight, wast thou not made the head of the tribes of Israel? And Jehovah anointed thee king over Israel;

units.leftText: and the LORD sent you on a journey, and said, ‘Go, and utterly destroy the sinners the Amalekites, and fight against them until they are consumed.’
units.rightText: and Jehovah sent thee on a journey, and said, Go, and utterly destroy the sinners the Amalekites, and fight against them until they be consumed.

units.leftText: Why then didn’t you obey the LORD’s voice, but took the plunder, and did that which was evil in the LORD’s sight?”
units.rightText: Wherefore then didst thou not obey the voice of Jehovah, but didst fly upon the spoil, and didst that which was evil in the sight of Jehovah?

units.leftText: Saul said to Samuel, “But I have obeyed the LORD’s voice, and have gone the way which the LORD sent me, and have brought Agag the king of Amalek, and have utterly destroyed the Amalekites.
units.rightText: And Saul said unto Samuel, Yea, I have obeyed the voice of Jehovah, and have gone the way which Jehovah sent me, and have brought Agag the king of Amalek, and have utterly destroyed the Amalekites.

units.leftText: But the people took of the plunder, sheep and cattle, the best of the devoted things, to sacrifice to the LORD your God in Gilgal.”
units.rightText: But the people took of the spoil, sheep and oxen, the chief of the devoted things, to sacrifice unto Jehovah thy God in Gilgal.

units.leftText: Samuel said, “Has the LORD as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the LORD’s voice? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to listen than the fat of rams.
units.rightText: And Samuel said, Hath Jehovah as great delight in burnt-offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of Jehovah? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.

units.leftText: For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as idolatry and teraphim. Because you have rejected the LORD’s word, he has also rejected you from being king.”
units.rightText: For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as idolatry and teraphim. Because thou hast rejected the word of Jehovah, he hath also rejected thee from being king.
leftNotes: 15:23 teraphim were household idols that may have been associated with inheritance rights to the household property.

units.leftText: Saul said to Samuel, “I have sinned; for I have transgressed the commandment of the LORD and your words, because I feared the people and obeyed their voice.
units.rightText: And Saul said unto Samuel, I have sinned; for I have transgressed the commandment of Jehovah, and thy words, because I feared the people, and obeyed their voice.

units.leftText: Now therefore, please pardon my sin, and turn again with me, that I may worship the LORD.”
units.rightText: Now therefore, I pray thee, pardon my sin, and turn again with me, that I may worship Jehovah.

units.leftText: Samuel said to Saul, “I will not return with you; for you have rejected the LORD’s word, and the LORD has rejected you from being king over Israel.”
units.rightText: And Samuel said unto Saul, I will not return with thee; for thou hast rejected the word of Jehovah, and Jehovah hath rejected thee from being king over Israel.

units.leftText: As Samuel turned around to go away, Saul grabbed the skirt of his robe, and it tore.
units.rightText: And as Samuel turned about to go away, Saul laid hold upon the skirt of his robe, and it rent.

units.leftText: Samuel said to him, “The LORD has torn the kingdom of Israel from you today, and has given it to a neighbor of yours who is better than you.
units.rightText: And Samuel said unto him, Jehovah hath rent the kingdom of Israel from thee this day, and hath given it to a neighbor of thine, that is better than thou.

units.leftText: Also the Strength of Israel will not lie nor repent; for he is not a man, that he should repent.”
units.rightText: And also the Strength of Israel will not lie nor repent; for he is not a man, that he should repent.

units.leftText: Then he said, “I have sinned; yet please honor me now before the elders of my people and before Israel, and come back with me, that I may worship the LORD your God.”
units.rightText: Then he said, I have sinned: yet honor me now, I pray thee, before the elders of my people, and before Israel, and turn again with me, that I may worship Jehovah thy God.

units.leftText: So Samuel went back with Saul; and Saul worshiped the LORD.
units.rightText: So Samuel turned again after Saul; and Saul worshipped Jehovah.

units.leftText: Then Samuel said, “Bring Agag the king of the Amalekites here to me!”
units.rightText: Then said Samuel, Bring ye hither to me Agag the king of the Amalekites. And Agag came unto him cheerfully. And Agag said, Surely the bitterness of death is past.

units.leftText: Samuel said, “As your sword has made women childless, so your mother will be childless among women!” Then Samuel cut Agag in pieces before the LORD in Gilgal.
units.rightText: And Samuel said, As thy sword hath made women childless, so shall thy mother be childless among women. And Samuel hewed Agag in pieces before Jehovah in Gilgal.

units.leftText: Then Samuel went to Ramah; and Saul went up to his house to Gibeah of Saul.
units.rightText: Then Samuel went to Ramah; and Saul went up to his house to Gibeah of Saul.

units.leftText: Samuel came no more to see Saul until the day of his death, but Samuel mourned for Saul. The LORD grieved that he had made Saul king over Israel.
units.rightText: And Samuel came no more to see Saul until the day of his death; for Samuel mourned for Saul: and Jehovah repented that he had made Saul king over Israel.

units.leftText: The LORD said to Samuel, “How long will you mourn for Saul, since I have rejected him from being king over Israel? Fill your horn with oil, and go. I will send you to Jesse the Bethlehemite, for I have provided a king for myself among his sons.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Samuel, How long wilt thou mourn for Saul, seeing I have rejected him from being king over Israel? fill thy horn with oil, and go: I will send thee to Jesse the Beth-lehemite; for I have provided me a king among his sons.

units.leftText: Samuel said, “How can I go? If Saul hears it, he will kill me.”
units.rightText: And Samuel said, How can I go? if Saul hear it, he will kill me. And Jehovah said, Take a heifer with thee, and say, I am come to sacrifice to Jehovah.

units.leftText: Call Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will show you what you shall do. You shall anoint to me him whom I name to you.”
units.rightText: And call Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will show thee what thou shalt do: and thou shalt anoint unto me him whom I name unto thee.

units.leftText: Samuel did that which the LORD spoke, and came to Bethlehem. The elders of the city came to meet him trembling, and said, “Do you come peaceably?”
units.rightText: And Samuel did that which Jehovah spake, and came to Beth-lehem. And the elders of the city came to meet him trembling, and said, Comest thou peaceably?

units.leftText: He said, “Peaceably; I have come to sacrifice to the LORD. Sanctify yourselves, and come with me to the sacrifice.” He sanctified Jesse and his sons, and called them to the sacrifice.
units.rightText: And he said, Peaceably; I am come to sacrifice unto Jehovah: sanctify yourselves, and come with me to the sacrifice. And he sanctified Jesse and his sons, and called them to the sacrifice.

units.leftText: When they had come, he looked at Eliab, and said, “Surely the LORD’s anointed is before him.”
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when they were come, that he looked on Eliab, and said, Surely Jehovah’s anointed is before him.

units.leftText: But the LORD said to Samuel, “Don’t look on his face, or on the height of his stature, because I have rejected him; for I don’t see as man sees. For man looks at the outward appearance, but the LORD looks at the heart.”
units.rightText: But Jehovah said unto Samuel, Look not on his countenance, or on the height of his stature; because I have rejected him: for Jehovah seeth not as man seeth; for man looketh on the outward appearance, but Jehovah looketh on the heart.

units.leftText: Then Jesse called Abinadab, and made him pass before Samuel. He said, “The LORD has not chosen this one, either.”
units.rightText: Then Jesse called Abinadab, and made him pass before Samuel. And he said, Neither hath Jehovah chosen this.

units.leftText: Then Jesse made Shammah to pass by. He said, “The LORD has not chosen this one, either.”
units.rightText: Then Jesse made Shammah to pass by. And he said, Neither hath Jehovah chosen this.

units.leftText: Jesse made seven of his sons to pass before Samuel. Samuel said to Jesse, “The LORD has not chosen these.”
units.rightText: And Jesse made seven of his sons to pass before Samuel. And Samuel said unto Jesse, Jehovah hath not chosen these.

units.leftText: Samuel said to Jesse, “Are all your children here?”
units.rightText: And Samuel said unto Jesse, Are here all thy children? And he said, There remaineth yet the youngest, and, behold, he is keeping the sheep. And Samuel said unto Jesse, Send and fetch him; for we will not sit down till he come hither.

units.leftText: He sent, and brought him in. Now he was ruddy, with a handsome face and good appearance. The LORD said, “Arise! Anoint him, for this is he.”
units.rightText: And he sent, and brought him in. Now he was ruddy, and withal of a beautiful countenance, and goodly to look upon. And Jehovah said, Arise, anoint him; for this is he.

units.leftText: Then Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the middle of his brothers. Then the LORD’s Spirit came mightily on David from that day forward. So Samuel rose up and went to Ramah.
units.rightText: Then Samuel took the horn of oil, and anointed him in the midst of his brethren: and the Spirit of Jehovah came mightily upon David from that day forward. So Samuel rose up, and went to Ramah.

units.leftText: Now the LORD’s Spirit departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the LORD troubled him.
units.rightText: Now the Spirit of Jehovah departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from Jehovah troubled him.

units.leftText: Saul’s servants said to him, “See now, an evil spirit from God troubles you.
units.rightText: And Saul’s servants said unto him, Behold now, an evil spirit from God troubleth thee.

units.leftText: Let our lord now command your servants who are in front of you to seek out a man who is a skillful player on the harp. Then when the evil spirit from God is on you, he will play with his hand, and you will be well.”
units.rightText: Let our lord now command thy servants, that are before thee, to seek out a man who is a skilful player on the harp: and it shall come to pass, when the evil spirit from God is upon thee, that he shall play with his hand, and thou shalt be well.

units.leftText: Saul said to his servants, “Provide me now a man who can play well, and bring him to me.”
units.rightText: And Saul said unto his servants, Provide me now a man that can play well, and bring him to me.

units.leftText: Then one of the young men answered and said, “Behold, I have seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite who is skillful in playing, a mighty man of valor, a man of war, prudent in speech, and a handsome person; and the LORD is with him.”
units.rightText: Then answered one of the young men, and said, Behold, I have seen a son of Jesse the Beth-lehemite, that is skilful in playing, and a mighty man of valor, and a man of war, and prudent in speech, and a comely person; and Jehovah is with him.

units.leftText: Therefore Saul sent messengers to Jesse, and said, “Send me David your son, who is with the sheep.”
units.rightText: Wherefore Saul sent messengers unto Jesse, and said, Send me David thy son, who is with the sheep.

units.leftText: Jesse took a donkey loaded with bread, a container of wine, and a young goat, and sent them by David his son to Saul.
units.rightText: And Jesse took an ass laden with bread, and a bottle of wine, and a kid, and sent them by David his son unto Saul.

units.leftText: David came to Saul and stood before him. He loved him greatly; and he became his armor bearer.
units.rightText: And David came to Saul, and stood before him: and he loved him greatly; and he became his armorbearer.

units.leftText: Saul sent to Jesse, saying, “Please let David stand before me, for he has found favor in my sight.”
units.rightText: And Saul sent to Jesse, saying, Let David, I pray thee, stand before me; for he hath found favor in my sight.

units.leftText: When the spirit from God was on Saul, David took the harp and played with his hand; so Saul was refreshed and was well, and the evil spirit departed from him.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when the evil spirit from God was upon Saul, that David took the harp, and played with his hand: so Saul was refreshed, and was well, and the evil spirit departed from him.

units.leftText: Now the Philistines gathered together their armies to battle; and they were gathered together at Socoh, which belongs to Judah, and encamped between Socoh and Azekah in Ephesdammim.
units.rightText: Now the Philistines gathered together their armies to battle; and they were gathered together at Socoh, which belongeth to Judah, and encamped between Socoh and Azekah, in Ephes-dammim.

units.leftText: Saul and the men of Israel were gathered together, and encamped in the valley of Elah, and set the battle in array against the Philistines.
units.rightText: And Saul and the men of Israel were gathered together, and encamped in the vale of Elah, and set the battle in array against the Philistines.

units.leftText: The Philistines stood on the mountain on the one side, and Israel stood on the mountain on the other side: and there was a valley between them.
units.rightText: And the Philistines stood on the mountain on the one side, and Israel stood on the mountain on the other side: and there was a valley between them.

units.leftText: A champion out of the camp of the Philistines named Goliath of Gath, whose height was six cubits and a span went out.
units.rightText: And there went out a champion out of the camp of the Philistines, named Goliath, of Gath, whose height was six cubits and a span.
leftNotes: 17:4 A cubit is the length from the tip of the middle finger to the elbow on a man’s arm, or about 18 inches or 46 centimeters. A span is the length from the tip of a man’s thumb to the tip of his little finger when his hand is stretched out (about half a cubit, or 9 inches, or 22.8 cm.) Therefore, Goliath was about 9 feet and 9 inches or 2.97 meters tall.

units.leftText: He had a helmet of bronze on his head, and he wore a coat of mail; and the weight of the coat was five thousand shekels of bronze.
units.rightText: And he had a helmet of brass upon his head, and he was clad with a coat of mail; and the weight of the coat was five thousand shekels of brass.
leftNotes: 17:5 A shekel is about 10 grams or about 0.35 ounces, so 5000 shekels is about 50 kilograms or 110 pounds.

units.leftText: He had bronze shin armor on his legs and a bronze javelin between his shoulders.
units.rightText: And he had greaves of brass upon his legs, and a javelin of brass between his shoulders.

units.leftText: The staff of his spear was like a weaver’s beam; and his spear’s head weighed six hundred shekels of iron. His shield bearer went before him.
units.rightText: And the staff of his spear was like a weaver’s beam; and his spear’s head weighed six hundred shekels of iron: and his shield-bearer went before him.
leftNotes: 17:7 A shekel is about 10 grams or about 0.35 ounces, so 600 shekels is about 6 kilograms or about 13 pounds.

units.leftText: He stood and cried to the armies of Israel, and said to them, “Why have you come out to set your battle in array? Am I not a Philistine, and you servants to Saul? Choose a man for yourselves, and let him come down to me.
units.rightText: And he stood and cried unto the armies of Israel, and said unto them, Why are ye come out to set your battle in array? am not I a Philistine, and ye servants to Saul? choose you a man for you, and let him come down to me.

units.leftText: If he is able to fight with me and kill me, then will we be your servants; but if I prevail against him and kill him, then you will be our servants and serve us.”
units.rightText: If he be able to fight with me, and kill me, then will we be your servants; but if I prevail against him, and kill him, then shall ye be our servants, and serve us.

units.leftText: The Philistine said, “I defy the armies of Israel today! Give me a man, that we may fight together!”
units.rightText: And the Philistine said, I defy the armies of Israel this day; give me a man, that we may fight together.

units.leftText: When Saul and all Israel heard those words of the Philistine, they were dismayed and greatly afraid.
units.rightText: And when Saul and all Israel heard those words of the Philistine, they were dismayed, and greatly afraid.

units.leftText: Now David was the son of that Ephrathite of Bethlehem Judah, whose name was Jesse; and he had eight sons. The man was an elderly old man in the days of Saul.
units.rightText: Now David was the son of that Ephrathite of Beth-lehem-judah, whose name was Jesse; and he had eight sons: and the man was an old man in the days of Saul, stricken in years among men.

units.leftText: The three oldest sons of Jesse had gone after Saul to the battle; and the names of his three sons who went to the battle were Eliab the firstborn, and next to him Abinadab, and the third Shammah.
units.rightText: And the three eldest sons of Jesse had gone after Saul to the battle: and the names of his three sons that went to the battle were Eliab the first-born, and next unto him Abinadab, and the third Shammah.

units.leftText: David was the youngest; and the three oldest followed Saul.
units.rightText: And David was the youngest; and the three eldest followed Saul.

units.leftText: Now David went back and forth from Saul to feed his father’s sheep at Bethlehem.
units.rightText: Now David went to and fro from Saul to feed his father’s sheep at Beth-lehem.

units.leftText: The Philistine came near morning and evening, and presented himself forty days.
units.rightText: And the Philistine drew near morning and evening, and presented himself forty days.

units.leftText: Jesse said to David his son, “Now take for your brothers an ephah of this parched grain and these ten loaves, and carry them quickly to the camp to your brothers;
units.rightText: And Jesse said unto David his son, Take now for thy brethren an ephah of this parched grain, and these ten loaves, and carry them quickly to the camp to thy brethren;
leftNotes: 17:17 1 ephah is about 22 liters or about 2/3 of a bushel

units.leftText: and bring these ten cheeses to the captain of their thousand; and see how your brothers are doing, and bring back news.”
units.rightText: and bring these ten cheeses unto the captain of their thousand, and look how thy brethren fare, and take their pledge.

units.leftText: Now Saul, and they, and all the men of Israel were in the valley of Elah, fighting with the Philistines.
units.rightText: Now Saul, and they, and all the men of Israel, were in the vale of Elah, fighting with the Philistines.

units.leftText: David rose up early in the morning and left the sheep with a keeper, and took the provisions and went, as Jesse had commanded him. He came to the place of the wagons as the army which was going out to the fight shouted for the battle.
units.rightText: And David rose up early in the morning, and left the sheep with a keeper, and took, and went, as Jesse had commanded him; and he came to the place of the wagons, as the host which was going forth to the fight shouted for the battle.

units.leftText: Israel and the Philistines put the battle in array, army against army.
units.rightText: And Israel and the Philistines put the battle in array, army against army.

units.leftText: David left his baggage in the hand of the keeper of the baggage and ran to the army, and came and greeted his brothers.
units.rightText: And David left his baggage in the hand of the keeper of the baggage, and ran to the army, and came and saluted his brethren.

units.leftText: As he talked with them, behold, the champion, the Philistine of Gath, Goliath by name, came up out of the ranks of the Philistines, and said the same words; and David heard them.
units.rightText: And as he talked with them, behold, there came up the champion, the Philistine of Gath, Goliath by name, out of the ranks of the Philistines, and spake according to the same words: and David heard them.

units.leftText: All the men of Israel, when they saw the man, fled from him and were terrified.
units.rightText: And all the men of Israel, when they saw the man, fled from him, and were sore afraid.

units.leftText: The men of Israel said, “Have you seen this man who has come up? He has surely come up to defy Israel. The king will give great riches to the man who kills him, and will give him his daughter, and will make his father’s house tax-free in Israel.”
units.rightText: And the men of Israel said, Have ye seen this man that is come up? surely to defy Israel is he come up: and it shall be, that the man who killeth him, the king will enrich him with great riches, and will give him his daughter, and make his father’s house free in Israel.

units.leftText: David spoke to the men who stood by him, saying, “What shall be done to the man who kills this Philistine and takes away the reproach from Israel? For who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God?”
units.rightText: And David spake to the men that stood by him, saying, What shall be done to the man that killeth this Philistine, and taketh away the reproach from Israel? for who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God?

units.leftText: The people answered him in this way, saying, “So shall it be done to the man who kills him.”
units.rightText: And the people answered him after this manner, saying, So shall it be done to the man that killeth him.

units.leftText: Eliab his oldest brother heard when he spoke to the men; and Eliab’s anger burned against David, and he said, “Why have you come down? With whom have you left those few sheep in the wilderness? I know your pride and the evil of your heart; for you have come down that you might see the battle.”
units.rightText: And Eliab his eldest brother heard when he spake unto the men; and Eliab’s anger was kindled against David, and he said, Why art thou come down? and with whom hast thou left those few sheep in the wilderness? I know thy pride, and the naughtiness of thy heart; for thou art come down that thou mightest see the battle.

units.leftText: David said, “What have I now done? Is there not a cause?”
units.rightText: And David said, What have I now done? Is there not a cause?

units.leftText: He turned away from him toward another, and spoke like that again; and the people answered him again the same way.
units.rightText: And he turned away from him toward another, and spake after the same manner: and the people answered him again after the former manner.

units.leftText: When the words were heard which David spoke, they rehearsed them before Saul; and he sent for him.
units.rightText: And when the words were heard which David spake, they rehearsed them before Saul; and he sent for him.

units.leftText: David said to Saul, “Let no man’s heart fail because of him. Your servant will go and fight with this Philistine.”
units.rightText: And David said to Saul, Let no man’s heart fail because of him; thy servant will go and fight with this Philistine.

units.leftText: Saul said to David, “You are not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him; for you are but a youth, and he a man of war from his youth.”
units.rightText: And Saul said to David, Thou art not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him; for thou art but a youth, and he a man of war from his youth.

units.leftText: David said to Saul, “Your servant was keeping his father’s sheep; and when a lion or a bear came and took a lamb out of the flock,
units.rightText: And David said unto Saul, Thy servant was keeping his father’s sheep; and when there came a lion, or a bear, and took a lamb out of the flock,

units.leftText: I went out after him, struck him, and rescued it out of his mouth. When he arose against me, I caught him by his beard, struck him, and killed him.
units.rightText: I went out after him, and smote him, and delivered it out of his mouth; and when he arose against me, I caught him by his beard, and smote him, and slew him.

units.leftText: Your servant struck both the lion and the bear. This uncircumcised Philistine shall be as one of them, since he has defied the armies of the living God.”
units.rightText: Thy servant smote both the lion and the bear: and this uncircumcised Philistine shall be as one of them, seeing he hath defied the armies of the living God.

units.leftText: David said, “The LORD, who delivered me out of the paw of the lion and out of the paw of the bear, will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine.”
units.rightText: And David said, Jehovah that delivered me out of the paw of the lion, and out of the paw of the bear, he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine. And Saul said unto David, Go, and Jehovah shall be with thee.

units.leftText: Saul dressed David with his clothing. He put a helmet of bronze on his head, and he clad him with a coat of mail.
units.rightText: And Saul clad David with his apparel, and he put a helmet of brass upon his head, and he clad him with a coat of mail.

units.leftText: David strapped his sword on his clothing and he tried to move, for he had not tested it. David said to Saul, “I can’t go with these, for I have not tested them.” Then David took them off.
units.rightText: And David girded his sword upon his apparel, and he assayed to go; for he had not proved it. And David said unto Saul, I cannot go with these; for I have not proved them. And David put them off him.

units.leftText: He took his staff in his hand, and chose for himself five smooth stones out of the brook, and put them in the pouch of his shepherd’s bag which he had. His sling was in his hand; and he came near to the Philistine.
units.rightText: And he took his staff in his hand, and chose him five smooth stones out of the brook, and put them in the shepherd’s bag which he had, even in his wallet; and his sling was in his hand: and he drew near to the Philistine.

units.leftText: The Philistine walked and came near to David; and the man who bore the shield went before him.
units.rightText: And the Philistine came on and drew near unto David; and the man that bare the shield went before him.

units.leftText: When the Philistine looked around and saw David, he disdained him; for he was but a youth, and ruddy, and had a good looking face.
units.rightText: And when the Philistine looked about, and saw David, he disdained him; for he was but a youth, and ruddy, and withal of a fair countenance.

units.leftText: The Philistine said to David, “Am I a dog, that you come to me with sticks?” The Philistine cursed David by his gods.
units.rightText: And the Philistine said unto David, Am I a dog, that thou comest to me with staves? And the Philistine cursed David by his gods.

units.leftText: The Philistine said to David, “Come to me, and I will give your flesh to the birds of the sky and to the animals of the field.”
units.rightText: And the Philistine said to David, Come to me, and I will give thy flesh unto the birds of the heavens, and to the beasts of the field.

units.leftText: Then David said to the Philistine, “You come to me with a sword, with a spear, and with a javelin; but I come to you in the name of the LORD of Armies, the God of the armies of Israel, whom you have defied.
